originalReview.title: Use the pretreatment skin presentation when planning after response
fairness: The resident must recognize the pretreatment inflammatory presentation and apply its continuing implications despite apparent breast and nodal response. This is a meaningful boundary against de-escalation after neoadjuvant treatment.
Mastectomy with axillary dissection is the defensible offered plan for the presented inflammatory, initially node-positive disease. The balanced matrix gives no component-frequency or length cue.

Importance: high breast oncology and ABSITE-style reasoning. Realism: the before/after record is coherent; the initially extensive rapid skin findings are necessary even though the table repeats some of them. This surgical task does not purport to describe all multimodal treatment.
suggestions: Retain the pretreatment skin extent and nodal confirmation; do not turn disappearance of the skin changes into permission for a different disease category.

originalReview.title: Resolve response and localization discordance before breast resection
fairness: Frozen PASS retained. Interpretation establishes that the palpable remnant and enhancing focus are one location, whereas the original marked bed is another; the learner must cover both relevant sites.
The key is defensible, and the balanced component frequencies prevent convergence. Rejecting a redundant pair requires interpreting the site record rather than reading option style.

Importance: high practical breast localization. Realism: marker/response discordance is credible. Localization of both sites is not a claim that enhancement alone defines microscopic disease or clear margins.
suggestions: Preserve the frozen version and the explicit distinction between the original marker and current palpable/enhancing focus.

originalReview.title: Bracket the malignant residual field rather than the MRI edge
fairness: The learner must interpret the sampled epithelial/necrotic finding as residual in-situ malignancy and incorporate its mapped extent beyond MRI enhancement. M-to-C is the defensible bracket within the expressly established conservation field.

Every option shares M and differs only at the other endpoint, so there is no majority-component cue. The pathological description at C supplies meaningful evidence; it is not a diagnosis label or an explanation that directly instructs the endpoint choice.
Importance: high breast conservation planning after therapy. Realism: the stated one-quadrant scope and established conservation decision repair the earlier missing operative scope.

The referenced image exists at apps/player/public/clinical-exhibits/batch2b-r2-b24-breast-map.png and was visually inspected. It is legible, explicitly constructed, and consistent with the text: M-E enhancement, M-C calcifications, P old palpable extent. This verifies the asset, not in-game rendering or microscopic margins.
suggestions: Preserve the explicit operative scope and spatial map. Keep the interpretation of the C specimen for the learner rather than adding a malignant-endpoint caption.

originalReview.title: DCIS: which inked surface is the final margin?
fairness: Original flag fully resolved: yes. Review versus re-excision no longer competes as sequential parts of one plan; all options now describe treatment.

The keyed plan is defensible among the offered choices: the resident must distinguish the main specimen edge from the separately oriented final cavity boundary, then apply the pure-DCIS/irradiation margin rule. The main-specimen 1-mm distance is a credible temptation rather than the final margin.

No exploitable zero-knowledge wording, grammar, length, absolute or convergence cue identified. Whole-breast irradiation appears in both the key and the closest competitor; the planned irradiation does not distinguish those choices. Completed reconciliation and the mammographic observations provide decision context rather than permission for a uniquely available action.

Completion mastectomy is a weaker competitor than posterior re-excision, but the specimen interpretation still makes the closest alternative substantive. No decision-critical omission or confident clinical error identified within this focused margin question.

Review scope for all 16 entries: judgments use only Presentation, Current update, Exhibit, Task and Options in after; titles and author reasoning are not learner evidence. Flags and handoffs establish history only. Difficulty is a qualitative PGY-2/3 prediction. No network/source re-verification, runtime/profile/feedback audit or clinical sign-off was performed. All drafts remain needs_clinician_review. Held F14 is excluded from this array and verdict/difficulty counts; its existing hold is unchanged.
suggestions: Retain the explicit specimen orientation and final external edge; do not simplify them back to a single margin summary.

Retain this exact version for independent clinical sign-off. If strengthening the mastectomy competitor, preserve the clear distinction between the original and final posterior boundaries and obtain a new review of the changed version.

originalReview.title: DCIS on both sides: choose the axillary staging plan

cues.phrase: On the left, separated areas occupy several breast regions
cues.why: Combined with the much larger left operation and localized right operation, this gives a nonmedical severity/laterality heuristic for choosing left staging. It does not prove the medical rule, but supports the key without knowing why the operation changes staging.

cues.phrase: the planned specimen includes the gland from the clavicle to the inframammary fold, while the skin envelope is retained for reconstruction
cues.why: This is a lengthy descriptive substitute for a familiar operation. Recognizing that operation supplies the conventional staging rule; paraphrasing its name does not create a second consequential inference. This is mainly a difficulty issue rather than a forbidden diagnosis cue.

fairness: Original flag fully resolved: yes for the confusing threatened-lymphatic-mapping premise. The item now uses a conventional operation-dependent staging decision instead of asserting an unspecified mapping compromise.

The left-only sentinel-node plan is the defensible best offered conventional answer for the described left mastectomy and right breast-conserving procedure in pure DCIS. No specific right-sided feature is supplied that makes an exception clearly applicable. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The normal bilateral nodal observations do not themselves exclude microscopic disease; retaining them is legitimate. The laterality set is balanced and does not create component-majority convergence.
Likely easy for PGY-2/3: identify the two operations and apply a familiar staging rule. Calling the operation by its specimen description adds decoding, not a clinically consequential second step.
suggestions: Use conventional operation names unless the exact specimen distinction changes the decision. Avoid hiding simple terminology inside longer prose to simulate difficulty.
Either obtain explicit acceptance for this foundational rule or use a source-supported, clinically meaningful staging dilemma with credible alternatives and enough data to resolve it.
Do not reintroduce the unsupported assumption that any oncoplastic procedure compromises subsequent mapping. Keep a genuine exception conditional on verified operative details and clinician review.

question.stem: Which localization plan should be arranged for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Localize the enhancing focus and original marker
answerChoices.rationale: The response has separated the palpable/enhancing remnant from the original marked bed. Current distribution and the known original site both need to be incorporated.

answerChoices.label: Localize the enhancing focus and palpable remnant
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Both targets describe the current lateral remnant, leaving the original marked bed unaccounted for. This is tempting if a clinical response is treated as disappearance of the known site.

answerChoices.label: Localize the pretreatment outline and original marker
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The original map and marker matter, but copying the entire old outline does not integrate the changed residual distribution.

answerChoices.label: Localize the pretreatment outline and palpable remnant
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This combines an unchanged original outline with examination rather than integrating the residual imaging and marked biopsy bed.

question.explanation: The response has separated the palpable/enhancing remnant from the original marked bed. Current distribution and the known original site both need to be incorporated. Both targets describe the current lateral remnant, leaving the original marked bed unaccounted for. This is tempting if a clinical response is treated as disappearance of the known site. The original map and marker matter, but copying the entire old outline does not integrate the changed residual distribution. This combines an unchanged original outline with examination rather than integrating the residual imaging and marked biopsy bed.
question.teachingPoint: The response has separated the palpable/enhancing remnant from the original marked bed. Current distribution and the known original site both need to be incorporated.

question.stem: Which breast and axillary operation should be discussed for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy with axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: The initial skin/lymphatic presentation establishes an inflammatory phenotype whose operative approach is not de-escalated merely because skin and nodal appearances respond.

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy with targeted axillary dissection
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Targeted de-escalation can be considered in selected noninflammatory settings; the pretreatment inflammatory presentation changes the axillary boundary here.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy with axillary dissection
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This recognizes the nodal issue but treats current response as sufficient to substitute breast conservation for the inflammatory-disease operation.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy with targeted axillary dissection
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This applies both breast and axillary de-escalation from a selected noninflammatory pathway to the wrong original phenotype.

question.explanation: The initial skin/lymphatic presentation establishes an inflammatory phenotype whose operative approach is not de-escalated merely because skin and nodal appearances respond. Targeted de-escalation can be considered in selected noninflammatory settings; the pretreatment inflammatory presentation changes the axillary boundary here. This recognizes the nodal issue but treats current response as sufficient to substitute breast conservation for the inflammatory-disease operation. This applies both breast and axillary de-escalation from a selected noninflammatory pathway to the wrong original phenotype.
question.teachingPoint: The initial skin/lymphatic presentation establishes an inflammatory phenotype whose operative approach is not de-escalated merely because skin and nodal appearances respond.

audit.reasons: A repeated 2-/3-mm width recognition adds little coverage beside the final-cavity PASS. The distance is already the rule in the lead-in, wider-threshold foils are weak and one-step. Consolidate future supply into the retained final-boundary PASS or the new positive-shave application without deleting any old definition. Exact v4 repeats the patient request for 5 mm in a task that already supplies 2 mm and planned irradiation; two wider-width foils and mastectomy do not create a second inference.

auditFindings.optionAndSequenceAudit: A repeated 2-/3-mm width recognition adds little coverage beside the final-cavity PASS. The distance is already the rule in the lead-in, wider-threshold foils are weak and one-step. Consolidate future supply into the retained final-boundary PASS or the new positive-shave application without deleting any old definition. question.stem: Which breast treatment plan is most appropriate for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Proceed with whole-breast irradiation
answerChoices.rationale: The additional oriented shave supplies the final posterior boundary. Its 2-mm negative edge meets the pure-DCIS/whole-breast-irradiation adequacy rule; the 1-mm main-specimen edge is not the final cavity edge.

answerChoices.label: Re-excise posteriorly, then use whole-breast irradiation
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is the near miss if the original 1-mm edge is carried forward without reconciling the separately oriented final margin.

answerChoices.label: Convert to completion mastectomy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: High grade and DCIS within an additional specimen do not by themselves negate the documented adequate final margins or mandate mastectomy.

question.explanation: The separately oriented external cavity-shave edge is the final posterior margin. Do not add specimen distances or carry forward the main-specimen measurement. The final negative margins are at least 2 mm and no residual calcifications are identified. For pure DCIS with planned whole-breast irradiation, this supports proceeding without routine wider re-excision. High grade does not create a different margin threshold here.

question.stem: Which axillary procedure should be planned for {patientName} at this operation?

answerChoices.label: Left sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The left specimen is a mastectomy despite retention of the skin envelope. Concurrent sentinel-node staging is ordinarily appropriate there; the right procedure is uncomplicated breast conservation.

answerChoices.label: Right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This applies staging to the conserving side while omitting the side whose operation can compromise later mapping. The core diagnosis is the same on both sides, but the operations differ.

answerChoices.label: Left and right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The bilateral diagnosis tempts symmetric staging, but uncomplicated pure-DCIS breast conservation does not routinely require sentinel-node biopsy.

answerChoices.label: No sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Pure DCIS and unremarkable nodal imaging do not remove the conventional staging consideration accompanying the left mastectomy.

question.explanation: Retaining the left skin envelope does not make removal of the gland a breast-conserving operation. Sentinel-node biopsy is ordinarily performed with that mastectomy because later mapping may be unreliable. The right localized excision is breast conservation, where routine axillary surgery for pure DCIS is generally omitted. The bilateral core diagnosis therefore does not imply bilateral axillary surgery.

projection.presentation: {patientName}, a 43-year-old woman, has bilateral core-biopsy findings of pure DCIS without identified invasion. On the left, separated areas occupy several breast regions; the planned specimen includes the gland from the clavicle to the inframammary fold, while the skin envelope is retained for reconstruction. On the right, the operation removes the localized DCIS with a rim of surrounding tissue and leaves the remaining breast. No axillary node is palpable; ultrasound on both sides shows oval nodes with retained fatty hila and thin uniform cortices.

fullCase.learningSummary: Routine lumpectomy for pure DCIS generally omits axillary surgery when invasion is not suspected.

audit.reasons: The conventional operation-dependent DCIS staging rule is important but these variants either repeat it, announce concern for invasion, or assert an unspecified future mapping compromise. Preserve the known preoperative rule and the F10 accepted fallback; do not imply a new independent basic-purpose acceptance. Exact v2 announces no invasion suspicion and feasible later mapping, then offers limited random sampling and ALND beside the routine omission key; its own scope excludes those foils.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: This reverses the accepted sequence and substitutes breast conservation for modified radical mastectomy.

question.stem: Which treatment sequence should be planned?

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy, adjuvant therapy, then observation
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Immediate surgery omits the required neoadjuvant systemic phase and postmastectomy radiation.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy, radiation, then systemic therapy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Breast-conserving surgery is not the definitive surgical approach for this diffuse skin-involving disease.

answerChoices.label: Radiation, lumpectomy, then systemic therapy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This reverses the accepted sequence and substitutes breast conservation for modified radical mastectomy.

question.explanation: Refer for multidisciplinary neoadjuvant systemic therapy, followed by modified radical mastectomy and postmastectomy radiation if the patient remains an operative candidate.

question.stem: Which next care plan best fits {patientName}'s current findings?

answerChoices.label: Repeat image-guided breast core biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The actual target was not represented by the core; resolve the imaging-pathology discordance rather than treat a missed-target benign result as exclusion.

answerChoices.label: Anti-inflammatory treatment with clinical reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The needle/marker and tissue do not explain the persistent imaged abnormality and clinical progression.

answerChoices.label: Skin punch biopsy with clinical reassessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Skin sampling may be complementary, but does not substitute for representative tissue from the unresolved parenchymal target.

question.explanation: Benign tissue is informative only when it accounts for the clinical and imaging target. A missed-target core requires further histologic assessment, with the technique selected jointly by breast imaging/pathology. Skin punch samples may add information but cannot independently clear the unsampled parenchymal lesion.
question.teachingPoint: Benign tissue is informative only when it accounts for the clinical and imaging target. answerChoices.label: Mastectomy of the affected breast
answerChoices.rationale: The separated residual invasive sites and extensive intervening/central in-situ field, not the absent palpable mass, make conservation unsuitable in this constructed distribution.

answerChoices.label: Oncoplastic resection of the mapped breast field

question.stem: Which endpoints should be requested for {patientName}'s image-guided bracketing?

answerChoices.label: Original marker to current enhancing edge
answerChoices.rationale: This includes the known original biopsy bed and current residual extent, rather than copying the full pretreatment boundary or omitting the medial known bed.

answerChoices.label: Original marker to pretreatment outer edge
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This preserves the known site but copies the larger pretreatment outer boundary instead of integrating the observed response.

answerChoices.label: Current enhancing edge to pretreatment outer edge
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Both endpoints lie lateral to the marked bed; this misreads the response map and omits the known medial biopsy site.

question.explanation: This includes the known original biopsy bed and current residual extent, rather than copying the full pretreatment boundary or omitting the medial known bed. question.stem: Which surgical-margin approach best addresses {patientName}'s 1-mm negative margin after breast-conserving surgery for pure DCIS?

answerChoices.label: Accept the margin without review
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The supported standard is 2 mm, so the narrower margin deserves individualized assessment.

answerChoices.label: Plan routine margin re-excision
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A margin below 2 mm does not require re-excision without considering case-specific factors.

answerChoices.label: Plan mastectomy for margin width
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A negative 1-mm margin is not by itself an indication for mastectomy.

question.explanation: A negative margin below 2 mm is assessed individually rather than assigned one automatic operation.

question.stem: Which axillary management strategy is most appropriate for {patientName}'s current operative plan?

answerChoices.label: Schedule sentinel-node biopsy at the forthcoming operation
answerChoices.rationale: The changed operation matters: sentinel-node assessment is ordinarily performed with standard mastectomy despite a pure-DCIS core result and unremarkable nodal imaging.

answerChoices.label: Schedule sentinel-node biopsy if final pathology reveals invasion
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Waiting for invasive final pathology is a credible breast-conservation sequence, but later mapping after standard mastectomy may be unreliable.

answerChoices.label: Omit sentinel-node biopsy from the overall treatment course
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Omission is ordinarily appropriate for uncomplicated DCIS breast conservation, not the conventional mastectomy setting now booked.

question.explanation: Pure DCIS on the core samples and unremarkable nodal imaging do not exclude occult invasion in the final breast specimen. Standard mastectomy can make later lymphatic mapping unreliable, so concurrent sentinel-node biopsy is ordinarily performed. A strategy appropriate for uncomplicated breast conservation should therefore be reconsidered when the breast operation changes to mastectomy.

answerChoices.label: Schedule sentinel-node biopsy at the forthcoming operation
answerChoices.rationale: The changed operation matters: sentinel-node assessment is ordinarily performed with standard mastectomy despite a pure-DCIS core result and unremarkable nodal imaging.

answerChoices.label: Schedule sentinel-node biopsy if final pathology reveals invasion
answerChoices.rationale: Waiting for invasive final pathology is a credible breast-conservation sequence, but later mapping after standard mastectomy may be unreliable.

answerChoices.label: Omit sentinel-node biopsy from the overall treatment course

decisionNodes.explanation: Pure DCIS on the core samples and unremarkable nodal imaging do not exclude occult invasion in the final breast specimen. Standard mastectomy can make later lymphatic mapping unreliable, so concurrent sentinel-node biopsy is ordinarily performed. A strategy appropriate for uncomplicated breast conservation should therefore be reconsidered when the breast operation changes to mastectomy.

decisionNodes.stem: Which treatment sequence should be planned for {patientName}'s confirmed inflammatory breast cancer?

answerChoices.label: Neoadjuvant therapy, surgery, then radiation
answerChoices.rationale: Refer for multidisciplinary neoadjuvant systemic therapy, followed by modified radical mastectomy and postmastectomy radiation if the patient remains an operative candidate.

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy, adjuvant therapy, then observation
answerChoices.rationale: Immediate surgery omits the required neoadjuvant systemic phase and postmastectomy radiation.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy, radiation, then systemic therapy
answerChoices.rationale: Breast-conserving surgery is not the definitive surgical approach for this diffuse skin-involving disease.

answerChoices.label: Radiation, lumpectomy, then systemic therapy
answerChoices.rationale: This reverses the accepted sequence and substitutes breast conservation for modified radical mastectomy.

question.stem: Which tissue-sampling plan should come first for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of parenchymal abnormality
answerChoices.rationale: Obtains tissue architecture from the imaged breast abnormality after an atypical cytologic sample; skin sampling can be adjunctive rather than a substitute for this target.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided aspiration of the parenchymal abnormality
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Repeats a cytologic approach without repairing the limitation in establishing an invasive tissue diagnosis and biomarker material.

answerChoices.label: Punch sampling of the involved breast skin
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can provide useful adjunctive information but is not the best substitute for sampling the imaged parenchymal abnormality in this record.

question.stem: Which axillary plan should be selected for {patientName}'s DCIS surgery?

exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Breast operation
items.value: The gland is being separated from the skin envelope and pectoral fascia across the entire breast footprint. The skin envelope is planned for reconstruction.

items.label: Tissue diagnosis and nodes
items.value: Mapped preoperative samples show DCIS without identified invasion. Examination and axillary ultrasound reveal no suspicious node.

answerChoices.label: Sentinel lymph-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: This gland-removal operation is a mastectomy despite retention of skin; sentinel staging is ordinarily coordinated with mastectomy for pure DCIS because later mapping may be unreliable.

answerChoices.label: Omit axillary surgery
answerChoices.rationale: Omission generally fits uncomplicated breast-conserving surgery for pure DCIS, not the described removal of the gland.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Omission generally fits uncomplicated breast-conserving surgery for pure DCIS, not the described removal of the gland.

answerChoices.label: Axillary lymph-node dissection
answerChoices.rationale: Pure DCIS with no suspicious node does not establish a need for routine axillary dissection; the staging issue is addressed with the sentinel pathway.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Pure DCIS with no suspicious node does not establish a need for routine axillary dissection; the staging issue is addressed with the sentinel pathway.

question.explanation: Retaining the skin envelope does not make complete gland removal a lumpectomy. For pure DCIS treated with mastectomy, sentinel staging is ordinarily coordinated with the operation because later mapping may be unreliable. Reassuring clinical nodes do not turn that operation into a breast-conserving pathway, and they do not justify axillary dissection.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic with new liver lesions after treatment of an ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The outside liver core contains metastatic breast carcinoma with sufficient viable tumor for additional assays. Its receptor studies have not been performed. The archived primary's receptor results are in the chart, and her systemic treatment is being reconsidered.
sourceLabels: Tests for Breast Cancer Biomarkers — NCI
case.learningSummary: The current core is adequate tumor tissue from the recurrence. Use it to reassess predictive receptor status rather than assume the original phenotype persists. Hereditary testing answers a separate question; no germline interpretation or metastatic drug regimen is scored here.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic after recurrence of previously ER-positive breast cancer. A bone core now contains metastatic breast carcinoma and is reported ER-negative, PR-negative and HER2-negative. Its processing record shows acid decalcification; the assay-validation record does not cover that process. A separate liver-core block contains viable metastatic breast carcinoma and was fixed without decalcification. The original breast block also contains viable carcinoma.
sourceLabels: Tests for Breast Cancer Biomarkers — NCI
ASCO metastatic breast cancer biomarker guideline, 2015
case.learningSummary: Receptor discordance can reflect a genuine biological change or a testing problem. The negative bone profile was obtained after a process outside the assay's validation. Test the available nondecalcified metastatic tissue to establish a more reliable current profile; repeating the primary answers a different chronological question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which laboratory plan should guide {patientName}'s current treatment reassessment?

answerChoices.label: Assay ER, PR and HER2 on the liver-core block
answerChoices.rationale: The nondecalcified current metastasis can reassess biology without inheriting the bone sample's unvalidated preanalytic process.

answerChoices.label: Use the reported bone-core receptor profile
answerChoices.rationale: A current specimen is normally valuable, but the negative profile cannot be treated as settled conversion when the actual decalcification process is outside assay validation and suitable alternative tissue exists.

answerChoices.rationale: It can confirm historical biology but cannot resolve whether the recurrence has genuinely changed phenotype.

steps: Interpret acid processing outside assay validation as a limitation on the negative metastatic profile, rather than proof of receptor conversion.
Choose the viable nondecalcified current metastasis instead of either accepting that profile or retreating to historical tumor biology.
authorGate.closestError: Accept the latest bone receptor report because current tissue should normally outrank the primary.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The negative bone profile followed an unvalidated decalcification process, while a nondecalcified current metastatic block is available.
authorGate.consequence: A technically uncertain negative profile can be mistaken for a biological treatment target change.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the bone sample had validated processing and reliable assays, a discordant current metastatic profile could legitimately guide treatment.
authorGate.deletionTest: Deleting the processing record removes the reason to question the current bone profile; deleting the liver provenance makes the selected current evidence unavailable. No missing assay is announced.
authorGate.cueAttack: All three plans concern the same tumor receptor evidence. Removed the germline foil and the named unperformed assay. Current bone, current liver and historical primary each offer a real but different evidentiary temptation.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Laboratory evidence plan before changing systemic treatment.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: current-versus-historical evidence must be reconciled with preanalytic reliability, not just tissue availability.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revision; no earlier feedback supplies the processing interpretation or choice.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision addresses every review cue. New concept version explicitly records the material addition of assay-validity interpretation; prior FSRS history is retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes specimen recency without interpreting processing-related uncertainty.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A current specimen is normally valuable, but the negative profile cannot be treated as settled conversion when the actual decalcification process is outside assay validation and suitable alternative tissue exists.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A technically reliable current metastatic assay can guide therapy even if it differs from the old primary.

distractorChecks.temptation: Escapes a technically questionable current result by returning to the familiar primary.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It can confirm historical biology but cannot resolve whether the recurrence has genuinely changed phenotype.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A question about the original assay itself would appropriately use the original block.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Removed the named missing assay, adequacy conclusion and unrelated germline option. Compared a current negative bone report, current nondecalcified metastatic tissue and historical primary tissue. The processing/validation record is the deciding evidence; current results can still govern if technically reliable. Removed software/scope language from feedback. ASCO specimen-processing guidance was directly verified and recorded with reserved rights.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Completion axillary review

steps: Identify the upfront clinically node-negative, limited positive-sentinel population.
Apply the actual nodal radiation component and morbidity goal to distinguish the supported omission pathway from extra surgery or inadequate field de-escalation.
authorGate.closestError: Treat the chest-wall field as equivalent to chest-wall plus regional nodal irradiation after mastectomy.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Only two sentinel nodes are involved and a regional nodal field is actually planned.
authorGate.consequence: A field mistake can remove the basis for omission, while automatically combining treatments adds avoidable morbidity.
authorGate.counterfactual: If regional nodal irradiation were ruled out, the offered radiation-only omission plan would no longer apply.
authorGate.deletionTest: The nodal burden and precise field are both necessary. The morbidity goal distinguishes an appropriate omission pathway from adding a redundant operation.
authorGate.cueAttack: All choices are concrete locoregional treatment plans. Repeat mapping is gone; radiation appears in every option, so the task's locoregional wording does not uniquely match the key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Postmastectomy locoregional treatment rather than repeated staging.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted fair moderate: the nearest field and surgery errors are credible; no harder rating is manufactured from an ordinary limited-node rule.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revised case; no unchanged PASS presentation is modified.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision broadens options to genuine regional-treatment strategies and keeps the reviewed population/field criteria explicit. Meaning remains the radiation-dependent axillary boundary.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies a positive-node surgery rule despite a radiation-supported omission population.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Adding dissection to the already applicable regional radiation plan is not required by these two positive sentinel nodes and works against the stated morbidity goal.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Residual disease after NST or a different higher-burden presentation can require a surgical regional approach.

distractorChecks.temptation: Transfers limited-node breast-conservation de-escalation to mastectomy while overlooking its different radiation context.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It drops the nodal-treatment component on which this mastectomy omission pathway depends.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A node-negative mastectomy patient with an independent chest-wall indication would present a different field question.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Retained upfront phase, limited node burden and actual nodal field. Replaced repeat staging with three locoregional treatment policies: the planned field, addition of dissection, or chest-wall-only de-escalation. A patient morbidity/control goal distinguishes gratuitous combined therapy from the supported radiation pathway. Current ASBrS population and NCI morbidity evidence were rechecked; no new clinical approval claimed.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Axillary response review
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 50-year-old woman, attends clinic after neoadjuvant treatment for noninflammatory breast cancer. The pretreatment surgeon documented a fixed cluster of axillary nodes, and a core contained metastatic carcinoma. A node was clipped. The cluster is no longer palpable, and current ultrasound shows smaller nodes. Definitive breast surgery is planned.

steps: Interpret the pretreatment fixed cluster as a different burden category from a mobile involved node.
Retain that original boundary when choosing the operation after response.
authorGate.closestError: Choose targeted de-escalation because the clipped node is now small and nonpalpable.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The original examination documented a fixed nodal cluster, not a single mobile involved node.
authorGate.consequence: Reclassifying baseline burden from the response examination can apply inadequately supported staging.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the original involved nodes were mobile cN1 and now clinically negative, optimized targeted/sentinel staging could become the key.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the original fixed-cluster record, the offered targeted strategy would become plausible. Current response creates the conflict rather than settling it.
authorGate.cueAttack: The task does not name a nodal category or a dissection indication. Technical options are concrete and comparable; the same targeted technique is the key in a different meaningful case.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Axillary operation during definitive surgery after neoadjuvant therapy.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: baseline burden must outweigh an apparently reassuring current response.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone; prior explanations from the converted-cN1 case are not part of this visible encounter.
authorGate.repairRecord: New distinct high-burden meaning, separate from uncomplicated post-NST staging; no frozen inflammatory phenotype is changed.

distractorChecks.temptation: Lets current response erase the original nodal category.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It imports a selected initially cN1 de-escalation strategy into a pretreatment fixed-cluster presentation with less established sentinel performance.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: The same technique is appropriate in selected initially mobile cN1, now clinically negative noninflammatory disease.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses the current normal-looking axilla as if it were an uncomplicated upfront staging case.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It both crosses the original burden boundary and omits the optimization used in selected initially node-positive settings.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An initially node-negative presentation is a different sentinel-staging setting.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Preserve exact PASS wording and payload despite optional suggestions. A mixed-case split is authorized by the manager; header/patient fields and the entire reviewed target node/question remain unchanged. Split-envelope composition is separately reported, not a new clinical approval.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Progressive breast swelling
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old woman, attends clinic with rapidly progressive right breast redness and pitting over much of the breast. Ultrasound shows a persistent irregular parenchymal area and thickened skin. Skin punch sections contain dermis with inflammation; the parenchymal area has not been sampled. There is no drainable collection.

case.learningSummary: The skin sample does not represent the parenchymal target. Arrange an image-guided breast core for tissue diagnosis and biomarker assessment. A skin biopsy can add information, but its inflammatory contents neither resolve that target nor establish that the broader presentation is benign. The original skin extent matters even though invasive carcinoma is confirmed on a breast core. In the nonmetastatic inflammatory setting, systemic therapy precedes modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiation. The case does not yet supply a treatment response or a reconstruction timetable.

decisionNodes.stem: Which tissue procedure should be arranged next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of the parenchymal area
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent breast target is distinct from the sampled dermis and requires representative tissue capable of establishing invasive carcinoma and treatment biomarkers.

answerChoices.label: Repeat punch biopsy of the erythematous skin
answerChoices.rationale: Skin sampling can be adjunctive, but repeating it does not substitute for histologic assessment of the visible parenchymal target.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided aspiration of the parenchymal area
answerChoices.rationale: A core is preferable for the required architecture and biomarker-capable tissue assessment when technically possible; aspiration is not drainage of a collection here.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: {patientName}'s breast core confirms invasive carcinoma; ER, PR and HER2 testing is complete. The pretreatment photographs show erythema and pitting across most of the breast, with progression documented before biopsy. Regional nodal sampling contains carcinoma, and systemic staging finds no distant metastasis. No cancer treatment has yet been given.

answerChoices.label: Systemic therapy, modified radical mastectomy, radiation
answerChoices.rationale: The original diffuse inflammatory presentation with confirmed nonmetastatic carcinoma calls for systemic treatment before the definitive breast/axillary operation and radiation.

answerChoices.rationale: It makes local radiation the initial step rather than the established systemic-first approach for this nonmetastatic presentation.

steps: Integrate rapid diffuse pretreatment skin involvement with invasive pathology and regional-only staging.
Apply the inflammatory systemic-first sequence rather than immediate surgery or radiation.
authorGate.closestError: Begin with mastectomy because the known disease is regionally resectable.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Documented pretreatment diffuse skin phenotype with invasive cancer and no distant spread.
authorGate.consequence: A localized surgery-first model is applied to the wrong clinical disease setting.
authorGate.counterfactual: A localized noninflammatory primary could make surgery first appropriate; distant metastasis would change the curative trimodality framework.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing skin chronology or distant staging changes the available sequence; biomarker completion allows treatment planning without inventing a regimen.
authorGate.cueAttack: Each option uses the same three modalities and differs only in phase order. Neither word novelty nor a uniquely complete multimodal key selects the answer.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial sequence of definitive multimodal treatment.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: distinguish an inflammatory phenotype from simply operable regional cancer using the original record.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: The first node feedback establishes diagnosis needs without giving this sequence. No hypothetical future response is treated as an observed response.
authorGate.repairRecord: Same sequence concept; repairs the original set's omitted-radiation and lumpectomy caricatures without touching the frozen B37-context variant.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes immediate resection of an operable primary before systemic treatment.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The operation is not ordinarily the first treatment for this pretreatment inflammatory presentation.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Selected noninflammatory resectable cancers may be treated with surgery first.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats extensive skin involvement as a reason to irradiate before systemic treatment.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It makes local radiation the initial step rather than the established systemic-first approach for this nonmetastatic presentation.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Different local-control or palliation circumstances require their own multidisciplinary sequence; this record does not establish one.

steps: Reconstruct the marker-to-malignant-target relationship from the original and localization records.
Use actual target representation to choose closure versus more imaging or tissue removal.
authorGate.closestError: Excise additional medial tissue merely because the top-hat marker is absent from the specimen.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The marker was separate before surgery, while all mapped target calcifications are in the oriented specimen.
authorGate.consequence: A marker-only shortcut can remove unnecessary tissue or misclassify true target failure in another case.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the original marker lay within the cluster and current imaging showed residual cluster with it, targeted further excision would replace closure.
authorGate.deletionTest: The original marker relationship is essential: delete it and absent marker plus visible calcifications leaves an unresolved discrepancy. Current imaging is needed to distinguish an unexplained missing marker from known target retrieval.
authorGate.cueAttack: Reversed the prior draft's explicitly retained target. Each plan is a realistic preclosure action. The key does not assert clear microscopic margins, and no sentence says 'the correct target has been removed'.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Disposition of the operative field after localization/specimen review.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: resist chasing a familiar marker when the longitudinal target relationship differs.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone clinic chart review; no new operating-room setting or executed local service is required.
authorGate.repairRecord: Preserves the N4r2 target-reconciliation concept. The original's current-localization sentence revealed the missed target; this new exact version requires longitudinal interpretation.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats marker retrieval as identical to malignant target retrieval even when their relation is documented differently.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It would chase the separately positioned marker despite current imaging confirmation of target retrieval.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A marker within a persisting proven target could appropriately guide further excision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses more pictures to compensate for a marker absence that is already explained by the original localization relation.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The supplied orthogonal specimen views and current breast image already resolve whether the mapped target was removed; further views do not establish microscopic margins.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An inadequately depicted specimen or unresolved target location would justify further imaging before an operative decision.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Review breast extent
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 57-year-old woman, attends clinic with a biopsy-proven left invasive carcinoma at 10 o'clock. Mammography and ultrasound show one localized lesion. MRI also shows a separate irregular enhancing focus at 4 o'clock. The radiologist can target both findings; only the 10-o'clock lesion has been sampled. The additional focus would change the planned breast resection.
sourceLabels: Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK
ASBrS breast conserving surgery resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: One proven cancer does not make every separate enhancing focus malignant. Sample the additional management-changing target before escalating the operation on its account, then assess whether its tissue result fits that target. A benign report is not independent of its target. The needle position and adipose specimen leave the irregular focus unrepresented. Resolve that focus with representative tissue before either dismissing it or using it to justify a larger cancer operation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic procedure should {patientName} undergo before the breast operation is changed?

answerChoices.label: Image-guided core biopsy of the 4-o'clock focus
answerChoices.rationale: The management-changing additional focus is not represented by the known 10-o'clock cancer sample.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided repeat core biopsy of the 10-o'clock lesion
answerChoices.rationale: More tissue from the proven primary would not establish the nature of the separate focus.

answerChoices.label: Short-interval contrast-enhanced breast MRI
answerChoices.rationale: It delays representative assessment of a suspicious focus that would alter the current operation.

decisionNodes.explanation: One proven cancer does not make every separate enhancing focus malignant. Sample the additional management-changing target before escalating the operation on its account, then assess whether its tissue result fits that target.
sourceLabels: Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should {patientName} receive for the 4-o'clock finding?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The 4-o'clock focus is sampled. Pathology shows mature adipose tissue and scant stroma. Archived needle images put the sampling notch posterior to the enhancing focus, and the postprocedure marker is in that same fat plane. Repeat targeted imaging still shows the irregular focus. {patientName}'s primary remains localized at 10 o'clock.

answerChoices.label: Repeat image-guided sampling of the 4-o'clock focus
answerChoices.rationale: The sample's location and contents do not represent the persisting target, so its benign result cannot settle that focus.

answerChoices.label: Interval breast imaging after the primary resection
answerChoices.rationale: The nonrepresentative sample has not resolved the additional suspicious focus before surgery is finalized.

answerChoices.label: Proceed to mastectomy for both mapped breast sites
answerChoices.rationale: The additional focus remains unproven, so this would treat uncertain extent as established separate malignancy.

case.learningSummary: A strong enhancement response does not settle the residual calcifications. authorGate.closestError: Choose a bracketed oncoplastic reduction because it appears able to remove more tissue than an ordinary lumpectomy.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Positive mapped sites span the central breast and every peripheral quadrant within a continuous calcified field.
authorGate.consequence: Treating diffuse disease as a set of focal targets can leave intervening malignancy or create an unsupported conservation plan.
authorGate.counterfactual: With a localized encompassable field or a few discrete appropriately resectable foci, conservation could again be considered.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the continuous all-quadrant map, mastectomy is not established. The small MRI remnant creates the meaningful conflicting signal. No breast-volume cutoff is invented.
authorGate.cueAttack: Both conservation choices explicitly attempt to encompass the current field, rather than knowingly excise old targets. No sentence supplies the conclusion that conservation is impossible.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Definitive breast resection after verified residual extent.

authorGate.repairRecord: One revision removes undocumented original foci, supplies a consistent current field and replaces both old-target-only foils with real current-field conservation attempts.

steps: Recognize that the final specimen contains a substantive invasive component.
Use the invasive-cancer margin standard rather than automatically extending the prior pure-DCIS rule.
authorGate.closestError: Order another re-excision because the DCIS distance remains below 2 mm.
authorGate.decidingObservation: An 8-mm invasive component is present and both components are off the final ink.
authorGate.consequence: Using the wrong framework can cause an unnecessary additional breast operation.
authorGate.counterfactual: If final lateral ink contained carcinoma, further lateral excision would again be favored.
authorGate.deletionTest: The invasive component is essential; remove it and the narrower pure-DCIS decision is individualized rather than the same categorical answer. Imaging clearance prevents a hidden separate target.
authorGate.cueAttack: The update gives measurements and ink observations, not 'adequate margins'. All choices are operations at the same stage. The earlier node's 2-mm counterfactual deliberately creates a credible carry-forward error, not the next key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Need for another breast operation after definitive re-excision pathology.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: applies a changed histologic framework despite the strongly rehearsed DCIS standard.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Later feedback does not reveal axillary or systemic-treatment answers. Each later currentUpdate is an outside-care chart event, not a result generated by an uninstalled service.
authorGate.repairRecord: New meaning under a new concept; do not transfer the old pure-DCIS FSRS history to this invasive-component decision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Carries the earlier DCIS framework forward after the definitive diagnosis changes.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It applies the pure-DCIS width requirement to an invasive carcinoma specimen despite absence of tumor on ink.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Pure DCIS with a clinically consequential close radial margin would require a different case-specific assessment; tumor on ink would favor excision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats two operations and persistent sub-2-mm distance as automatic failure of conservation.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A close but ink-negative DCIS component accompanying invasive cancer is not a stand-alone indication for mastectomy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Diffuse residual malignant disease or unresectable positive margins would change the operation.

steps: Interpret receptor status together with the substantial primary and proven regional disease.
Select combined preoperative systemic therapy rather than moving either the whole regimen or its chemotherapy component until after surgery.
authorGate.closestError: Choose the surgery-first plan because all visible disease appears operable.
authorGate.decidingObservation: A 4.3-cm HER2-positive primary has biopsy-proven mobile nodal metastasis before any treatment.
authorGate.consequence: An operability shortcut can bypass an established response-guided systemic-first pathway.
authorGate.counterfactual: A small node-negative primary would change the timing balance toward an appropriate surgery-first pathway.
authorGate.deletionTest: Regional burden and original biology are needed to prefer a neoadjuvant course; no option can be chosen by HER2 word matching because every plan includes the same targeted drugs.
authorGate.cueAttack: Removed the endocrine foil. All labels contain surgery, chemotherapy and trastuzumab/pertuzumab, differing in phase and grouping rather than key-only biomarker vocabulary.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial sequence of the same cancer-treatment components.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted fair moderate: a real surgery-first competitor and a recognizable targeted-de-escalation sequencing error replace an inapplicable endocrine choice.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revised node. The PASSED later adjuvant node is isolated with its exact original wording.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision fixes the unique HER2 label and endocrine filler without claiming a new independent PASS or adding drug doses.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses resectability to favor immediate surgery despite the response-guided neoadjuvant setting.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It postpones the established combined systemic strategy until after resection in this node-positive substantial primary.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An appropriately selected small node-negative cancer may be managed with upfront surgery.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats the predictive target as sufficient reason to postpone chemotherapy until after surgery.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It defers the cytotoxic component instead of delivering the preferred combined preoperative regimen; trial exploration of chemotherapy-free blockade does not establish this as the routine choice here.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A separately reviewed de-escalation protocol or a genuine chemotherapy contraindication would require a different treatment question.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: All options now contain chemotherapy, trastuzumab/pertuzumab and surgery. The alternatives differ in grouping/timing, eliminating the key-only HER2 match and inapplicable endocrine foil. NCI explicitly supports combined systemic treatment before surgery and describes chemotherapy-free dual-blockade trial exploration; exact doses/cycles are not authored. Split the later PASS adjuvant node rather than change its text.

authorGate.closestError: Replace dissection with axillary radiation because the deposit is small and was removed in a mapped node.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The 0.9-mm metastasis remains after neoadjuvant therapy, not at an upfront conservation operation.
authorGate.consequence: Cross-population extrapolation can omit the regional operation recommended for residual disease.
authorGate.counterfactual: The analogous limited sentinel finding at upfront conservation could support no completion operation; an adequate ypN0 result after NST also changes the decision.
authorGate.deletionTest: Both measured burden and treatment chronology matter. Palpation is corrected to nodes and cannot overrule the positive specimen.
authorGate.cueAttack: Three real axillary treatment policies replace repeated completed staging. Shared whole-breast treatment stays outside options, so the key is not uniquely comprehensive or uniquely linked to radiation wording.

The positive residual-micrometastasis indication was rechecked in the February 2026 ASBrS guide; Melissa review remains pending.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next care plan best fits {patientName}'s current findings?

answerChoices.label: Repeat image-guided breast core biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The actual target was not represented by the core; resolve the imaging-pathology discordance rather than treat a missed-target benign result as exclusion.

answerChoices.label: Anti-inflammatory treatment with clinical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The needle/marker and tissue do not explain the persistent imaged abnormality and clinical progression.

answerChoices.label: Skin punch biopsy with clinical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Skin sampling may be complementary, but does not substitute for representative tissue from the unresolved parenchymal target.

decisionNodes.explanation: Benign tissue is informative only when it accounts for the clinical and imaging target. Skin punch samples may add information but cannot independently clear the unsampled parenchymal lesion.

decisionNodes.stem: Which breast and axillary operation should be discussed for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy with axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: The initial skin/lymphatic presentation establishes an inflammatory phenotype whose operative approach is not de-escalated merely because skin and nodal appearances respond.

answerChoices.label: Mastectomy with targeted axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: Targeted de-escalation can be considered in selected noninflammatory settings; the pretreatment inflammatory presentation changes the axillary boundary here.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy with axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes the nodal issue but treats current response as sufficient to substitute breast conservation for the inflammatory-disease operation.

answerChoices.label: Lumpectomy with targeted axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: This applies both breast and axillary de-escalation from a selected noninflammatory pathway to the wrong original phenotype.

decisionNodes.stem: Which breast treatment plan is most appropriate for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Proceed with whole-breast irradiation
answerChoices.rationale: The additional oriented shave supplies the final posterior boundary. Its 2-mm negative edge meets the pure-DCIS/whole-breast-irradiation adequacy rule; the 1-mm main-specimen edge is not the final cavity edge.

answerChoices.label: Re-excise posteriorly, then use whole-breast irradiation
answerChoices.rationale: This is the near miss if the original 1-mm edge is carried forward without reconciling the separately oriented final margin.

answerChoices.label: Convert to completion mastectomy
answerChoices.rationale: High grade and DCIS within an additional specimen do not by themselves negate the documented adequate final margins or mandate mastectomy.

decisionNodes.explanation: The separately oriented external cavity-shave edge is the final posterior margin. Do not add specimen distances or carry forward the main-specimen measurement. The final negative margins are at least 2 mm and no residual calcifications are identified. For pure DCIS with planned whole-breast irradiation, this supports proceeding without routine wider re-excision. High grade does not create a different margin threshold here.

answerChoices.label: Left sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The left specimen is a mastectomy despite retention of the skin envelope. Concurrent sentinel-node staging is ordinarily appropriate there; the right procedure is uncomplicated breast conservation.

answerChoices.label: Right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: This applies staging to the conserving side while omitting the side whose operation can compromise later mapping. The core diagnosis is the same on both sides, but the operations differ.

answerChoices.label: Left and right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The bilateral diagnosis tempts symmetric staging, but uncomplicated pure-DCIS breast conservation does not routinely require sentinel-node biopsy.

answerChoices.label: No sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Pure DCIS and unremarkable nodal imaging do not remove the conventional staging consideration accompanying the left mastectomy.

rankedConcepts.title: Axillary surgery depends on initial burden, treatment phase and radiation
rankedConcepts.relevance: High practical and general-surgery testing relevance; common errors cross otherwise similar de-escalation populations.
rankedConcepts.decision: Choose optimized staging, omit completion surgery or perform dissection in the correct population.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Original mobile versus fixed nodes, biopsy/clip record, treatment chronology, sentinel specimen results and actual radiation fields.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Treat every positive node or every post-treatment normal ultrasound with the same rule.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Unnecessary axillary morbidity or inadequately supported regional treatment.
rankedConcepts.gap: Substantive invasive-cancer axillary decisions were absent; DCIS sentinel rows are not equivalent coverage.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Final margins and the correct invasive versus pure-DCIS framework
rankedConcepts.relevance: High: prevents both residual local disease and unnecessary reoperations.
rankedConcepts.decision: Determine the actual final boundary and whether an additional breast excision is indicated.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Oriented main specimen and new external shave, ink involvement, represented residual parenchyma and final invasive component.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Use a main-specimen distance as the final margin, or carry the pure-DCIS 2-mm rule into invasive carcinoma with DCIS.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Leave an involved radial boundary or perform a preventable extra operation.
rankedConcepts.gap: Existing three width-recognition siblings duplicate one rule; the retained F01 final-negative boundary and new final-positive boundary are meaningful contrasts.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Tumor biology selects sequence and residual invasive disease changes adjuvant planning
rankedConcepts.relevance: High: consequential surgeon/oncologist handoff decisions without drug-dose trivia.
rankedConcepts.decision: Recommend neoadjuvant HER2-directed treatment and identify the residual-invasive adjuvant indication.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: ER/PR/HER2 assays, primary and nodal extent, actual prior taxane/trastuzumab treatment and definitive invasive versus DCIS pathology.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Equate operability with surgery first or treat small residual invasive disease as complete response.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Lose response-guided planning or miss a supported adjuvant option.
rankedConcepts.gap: Noninflammatory subtype-driven sequencing and response-adapted adjuvant therapy were missing; the inflammatory sequence is a different construct.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Post-NST residual field, not enhancement alone, determines local surgery
rankedConcepts.relevance: High: imaging/tissue integration changes localization and operation.
rankedConcepts.decision: Identify the unsolved field for sampling, then apply verified residual distribution to surgery.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Original proven target, current enhancement, broader calcifications and mapped samples.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Use MRI response as a microscopic disease-clearance map or treat all multifocal disease as mandatory mastectomy.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Under-resect residual disease or overstate a conservation contraindication.
rankedConcepts.gap: Retain B2B10/B2B24/B2B08; improve easy siblings and do not change the frozen first node to repair its rehearsed companion.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Additional-focus verification and specimen/marker provenance
rankedConcepts.relevance: High operative safety and preoperative decision relevance.
rankedConcepts.decision: Verify a management-changing target and reconcile whether the intended lesion is actually represented.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Two site identities, needle notch and specimen contents, original marker position, oriented specimen/current breast images.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Let a benign wrong-target sample or any visible marker settle the cancer target.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Unnecessary mastectomy, missed additional malignancy or unnecessary extra excision.
rankedConcepts.gap: Retain B37; use a different noninflammatory adequacy context and repair N4 marker-key disclosure.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Inflammatory phenotype: representative tissue and systemic-first local-treatment sequence
rankedConcepts.relevance: High: changes the whole treatment sequence despite apparent resectability or response.
rankedConcepts.decision: Obtain the relevant tissue, then choose systemic therapy before definitive breast/axillary surgery and radiation.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Rapid diffuse pretreatment skin record, sampled dermis versus parenchyma, invasive pathology and distant staging.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Treat skin inflammation as a representative benign breast diagnosis or apply localized surgery first.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Delay diagnosis or apply the wrong therapeutic phase.
rankedConcepts.gap: Many cosmetic recognition pairs; retain exact B37/B37-context and B2B08 while consolidating repetition.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: DCIS: breast operation and credible invasion/mapping concerns determine axillary staging
rankedConcepts.relevance: High foundational surgical rule with a documented difficulty deficit.
rankedConcepts.decision: Plan conventional sentinel surgery when the planned operation requires it, before the operation begins.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Actual breast operation, pathology concern for invasion, node findings and a verified delayed-mapping plan.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Assume no invasion in a core rules out occult invasion, or decide a preoperative plan as if a new intra-op finding had appeared.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Miss an opportunity for reliable staging or add unnecessary axillary surgery.
rankedConcepts.gap: F10 remains accepted REVISE, not basicAccepted or PASS. N4 intra-op quality park remains. A genuinely harder additional staging dilemma is not manufactured.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Paget: represent the skin target and evaluate the underlying breast
rankedConcepts.relevance: High recognition and local-treatment planning relevance; avoid repeated stereotyped stems.
rankedConcepts.decision: Sample the actual persistent epidermal target and subsequently establish underlying extent.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Persistent unilateral nipple lesion, what tissue a prior core represented, adequate skin pathology and conventional imaging.
rankedConcepts.closestError: A benign parenchymal core or normal mammography resolves the nipple lesion.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Miss nipple disease or choose an operation without assessing underlying carcinoma.
rankedConcepts.gap: Representative-biopsy rewrite supplied. Two attempted extent/resection drafts were removed after cue/difficulty checks; the operation gap remains explicit.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Current recurrent-tumor evidence versus historical primary biology
rankedConcepts.decision: Choose current tumor tissue for predictive biomarker reassessment before treatment replanning.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Viable recurrent tumor, archived primary assays and current missing receptor studies.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Assume the primary phenotype persists or substitute inherited-susceptibility testing for tumor receptor assays.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Use the wrong predictive phenotype for current treatment.
rankedConcepts.gap: New coverage; no germline interpretation or evolving metastatic regimen ranking.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Radiation after conservation and radiation-dependent surgical de-escalation
rankedConcepts.relevance: High: local surgery, patient goals and actual radiation fields must agree.
rankedConcepts.decision: Distinguish a committed nodal field, whole-breast radiation and a patient-specific reirradiation assessment.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Actual specialist plan and prior treatment records, not an unsupported author eligibility label.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Treat prior radiation as an absolute universal prohibition, or chest-wall-only treatment as regional nodal irradiation.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Misapply conservation or axillary omission criteria.
rankedConcepts.gap: Partially covered. Universal close-margin/RT-omission rules are withheld; no exact RT regimen or delay is invented.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Anatomic extent, regional versus distant disease and stage-to-goal distinctions
rankedConcepts.relevance: High testing relevance, but exact stage labeling should change a practical decision.
rankedConcepts.decision: Apply tissue-proven extent to a real treatment goal rather than decode a report label.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Original skin phenotype, regional tissue sampling and distant staging.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Let current response erase pretreatment phenotype or infer stage from a small residual focus alone.
rankedConcepts.gap: Applied extent boundaries covered; no standalone exact TNM/prognostic staging table item authored. Third-party AJCC tables embedded in NCI were not copied or used as a corpus.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Surveillance versus a new diagnostic question after treatment
rankedConcepts.relevance: Practical ambulatory relevance; pure protocol recall needs a credible competing error.
rankedConcepts.decision: Use clinical/breast surveillance in asymptomatic patients and investigate meaningful new findings separately.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Symptoms, examination, treatment history and actual breast surveillance status.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Use routine systemic imaging as reassurance or apply an asymptomatic rule to a new finding.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Unnecessary testing or delayed assessment of recurrence.
rankedConcepts.gap: Source-survey gap remains unfilled: no hard supported competing-symptom case or exact first-surveillance interval was authored.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

rankedConcepts.title: Reconstruction, axillary anatomy and treatment morbidity
rankedConcepts.relevance: Important surgical topic, lower priority than the uncovered management boundaries above.
rankedConcepts.decision: Plan reconstruction and manage procedure-related deficits in the context of oncologic treatment.
rankedConcepts.rawEvidence: Actual operative anatomy, nerve function, skin involvement and radiation plan.
rankedConcepts.closestError: Import an unsourced exact reconstruction interval or turn nerve-name recall into a cosmetic two-step item.
rankedConcepts.consequence: Unsupported technical teaching or poor treatment coordination.
rankedConcepts.gap: Not authored. A permitted technical source and a consequential decision with credible competitors are still needed; no ICU/ED setting proposal is required.
rankedConcepts.testingWeightBasis: Qualitative owner-directed editorial assessment; no exam-frequency or measured-difficulty claim.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Recurrence treatment review
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic with new liver lesions after treatment of an ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The outside liver core contains metastatic breast carcinoma with sufficient viable tumor for additional assays. Its receptor studies have not been performed. The archived primary's receptor results are in the chart, and her systemic treatment is being reconsidered.
sourceLabels: Tests for Breast Cancer Biomarkers — NCI
case.learningSummary: The current core is adequate tumor tissue from the recurrence. Use it to reassess predictive receptor status rather than assume the original phenotype persists. Hereditary testing answers a separate question; no germline interpretation or metastatic drug regimen is scored here.

decisionNodes.stem: Which laboratory assessment should guide {patientName}'s current tumor-receptor reassessment?

answerChoices.label: ER, PR and HER2 testing on the liver core
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate current tumor can establish the recurrence's predictive phenotype; the archived primary does not prove that phenotype is unchanged.

answerChoices.rationale: It reassesses the historical primary rather than establishing the present metastatic tumor's phenotype.

answerChoices.rationale: A germline panel addresses inherited susceptibility, not expression of predictive receptors in the current carcinoma.

steps: Distinguish current viable recurrent tumor from an archived primary and germline blood evidence.
Select the specimen and assays that can establish the current treatment phenotype.
authorGate.closestError: Reuse or repeat the original tumor's receptor tests as proof of current metastatic biology.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The current liver core contains sufficient viable metastatic tumor but lacks receptor assays.
authorGate.consequence: Historical biomarker assumptions may direct treatment toward the wrong phenotype.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the current core lacked viable tumor, current-tissue testing could not be ordered as a complete answer without obtaining an adequate sample.
authorGate.deletionTest: Specimen chronology and adequacy are necessary; liver lesion sizes and prognostic statistics would not change the decision and are omitted.
authorGate.cueAttack: All options name concrete laboratory assessments with waits. The two receptor panels are identically worded except specimen, so no assay-name novelty selects the key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Predictive laboratory assessment before systemic-treatment replanning.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate: distinguishes current somatic phenotype, historical evidence and inherited susceptibility without regimen trivia.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone current-recurrence case; no earlier feedback announces a changed receptor result.
authorGate.repairRecord: New tumor-biology evidence identity; germline interpretation remains owned by oncology-genetics-principles and is not scored.

distractorChecks.temptation: Assumes receptor results remain fixed because the origin is still breast carcinoma.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It reassesses the historical primary rather than establishing the present metastatic tumor's phenotype.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A disputed or technically inadequate original assay may require archival review for that separate question.

distractorChecks.temptation: Confuses inherited cancer biology with the current tumor's treatment phenotype.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A germline panel addresses inherited susceptibility, not expression of predictive receptors in the current carcinoma.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A hereditary-risk indication warrants its own genetics assessment; it does not replace tumor receptor testing.
