case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Completion axillary review
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 62-year-old woman, attends clinic after upfront mastectomy and sentinel biopsy for a 2.8-cm noninflammatory invasive cancer. Her axilla was clinically negative before surgery. Two of four sentinel nodes contain metastases; there is no gross extranodal disease. The radiation oncologist has planned postmastectomy chest-wall and regional nodal irradiation, and systemic therapy is planned.
sourceLabels: ASBrS axillary management resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: Mastectomy does not impose an unconditional completion-ALND rule. In selected upfront cases with limited positive sentinel burden, planned regional nodal irradiation can support omission. This is a radiation-dependent decision and should not be applied to post-NST residual nodes.

decisionNodes.stem: Which further axillary operation should be recommended for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: No completion axillary operation
answerChoices.rationale: Selected upfront mastectomy patients with one or two positive sentinel nodes can omit ALND when the adjuvant plan includes regional nodal irradiation.

answerChoices.label: Completion level I–II axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: It treats mastectomy plus any positive sentinel finding as an unconditional ALND requirement, despite the stated limited burden and nodal irradiation.

answerChoices.label: Repeat sentinel mapping and axillary sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The completed representative sentinel procedure already establishes the relevant limited burden; repeat staging is not a substitute for interpreting that information.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Progressive breast swelling
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old woman, attends clinic with rapidly progressive right breast redness and pitting over much of the breast. Ultrasound shows a persistent irregular parenchymal area and thickened skin. Skin punch sections contain dermis with inflammation; the parenchymal area has not been sampled. There is no drainable collection.
sourceLabels: Inflammatory Breast Cancer — NCI
Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK
Inflammatory Breast Cancer Treatment — NCI
ASBrS breast conserving surgery resource guide, February 2026
ASBrS axillary management resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: The skin sample does not represent the parenchymal target. Arrange an image-guided breast core for tissue diagnosis and biomarker assessment. A skin biopsy can add information, but its inflammatory contents neither resolve that target nor establish that the broader presentation is benign. The original skin extent matters even though invasive carcinoma is confirmed on a breast core. In the nonmetastatic inflammatory setting, systemic therapy precedes modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiation. The case does not yet supply a treatment response or a reconstruction timetable.

decisionNodes.stem: Which tissue procedure should be arranged next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of the parenchymal area
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent breast target is distinct from the sampled dermis and requires representative tissue capable of establishing invasive carcinoma and treatment biomarkers.

answerChoices.label: Repeat punch biopsy of the erythematous skin
answerChoices.rationale: Skin sampling can be adjunctive, but repeating it does not substitute for histologic assessment of the visible parenchymal target.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided aspiration of the parenchymal area
answerChoices.rationale: A core is preferable for the required architecture and biomarker-capable tissue assessment when technically possible; aspiration is not drainage of a collection here.

steps: Integrate rapid diffuse pretreatment skin involvement with invasive pathology and regional-only staging.
Apply the inflammatory systemic-first sequence rather than immediate surgery or radiation.
authorGate.closestError: Begin with mastectomy because the known disease is regionally resectable.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Documented pretreatment diffuse skin phenotype with invasive cancer and no distant spread.
authorGate.consequence: A localized surgery-first model is applied to the wrong clinical disease setting.
authorGate.counterfactual: A localized noninflammatory primary could make surgery first appropriate; distant metastasis would change the curative trimodality framework.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing skin chronology or distant staging changes the available sequence; biomarker completion allows treatment planning without inventing a regimen.
authorGate.cueAttack: Each option uses the same three modalities and differs only in phase order. Neither word novelty nor a uniquely complete multimodal key selects the answer.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial sequence of definitive multimodal treatment.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: distinguish an inflammatory phenotype from simply operable regional cancer using the original record.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: The first node feedback establishes diagnosis needs without giving this sequence. No hypothetical future response is treated as an observed response.
authorGate.repairRecord: Same sequence concept; repairs the original set's omitted-radiation and lumpectomy caricatures without touching the frozen B37-context variant.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes immediate resection of an operable primary before systemic treatment.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The operation is not ordinarily the first treatment for this pretreatment inflammatory presentation.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Selected noninflammatory resectable cancers may be treated with surgery first.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats extensive skin involvement as a reason to irradiate before systemic treatment.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It makes local radiation the initial step rather than the established systemic-first approach for this nonmetastatic presentation.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Different local-control or palliation circumstances require their own multidisciplinary sequence; this record does not establish one.

constructedObservations.basis: Fictional exact patient/biopsy/operative observations, not empirical frequencies or newly asserted treatment cutoffs. The rules interpreting them map to the atomic claims below.

statementMapping.numericalBasis: Ages, lesion measurements and specimen distances are constructed observations. Any decision threshold (DCIS 2 mm, limited positive-node populations, optimized sentinel retrieval) is supported by a specifically mapped source. No exact probability, drug dose or waiting time is authored.

node.stem: Which operative plan should be selected for {patientName} before closure?

answerChoices.label: Targeted re-excision with specimen radiography
answerChoices.rationale: The retrieved coil is the old benign marker, not proof of malignant-target removal. The residual target is medial and needs imaging confirmation after additional excision.

answerChoices.label: Repeat orthogonal views of the oriented specimen
answerChoices.rationale: A different view of the removed specimen cannot remove the target demonstrably retained in the breast. The marker identity mismatch requires target-directed excision.

answerChoices.label: Complete closure and await permanent histologic margins
answerChoices.rationale: Margin assessment of the removed tissue does not establish removal of a different target still visible in the breast.

node.explanation: The coil and top-hat markers represent different biopsy sites. The first specimen contains the old benign marker; imaging places the DCIS-associated marker and calcifications medial to the cavity. Remove tissue directed at that retained target and confirm the new specimen radiographically. Target confirmation does not establish the final microscopic margin width.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Review breast extent
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 57-year-old woman, attends clinic with a biopsy-proven left invasive carcinoma at 10 o'clock. Mammography and ultrasound show one localized lesion. MRI also shows a separate irregular enhancing focus at 4 o'clock. The radiologist can target both findings; only the 10-o'clock lesion has been sampled. The additional focus would change the planned breast resection.
sourceLabels: Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK
ASBrS breast conserving surgery resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: One proven cancer does not make every separate enhancing focus malignant. Sample the additional management-changing target before escalating the operation on its account, then assess whether its tissue result fits that target. A benign report is not independent of its target. The needle position and adipose specimen leave the irregular focus unrepresented. Resolve that focus with representative tissue before either dismissing it or using it to justify a larger cancer operation.

case.learningSummary: One proven cancer does not make every separate enhancing focus malignant. authorGate.closestError: Treat the benign pathology label as evidence about the enhancing focus.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The sampling notch and marker were posterior to the persistent target in fat.
authorGate.consequence: Either missed additional disease or unnecessary mastectomy can follow a provenance error.
authorGate.counterfactual: A correctly positioned notch with representative benign tissue explaining the imaging would permit a benign-concordant pathway.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the new acquisition and specimen contents, the earlier task merely called for biopsy; this update earns a separate adequacy decision.
authorGate.cueAttack: The update describes positions without saying 'missed target'. Three care plans differ at the real point of uncertainty; the key does not add a unique list of general cautions.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Disposition of the unresolved additional focus after tissue sampling.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: neither benign-label reassurance nor automatic malignant attribution is justified.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Earlier feedback says to sample the focus, not that any subsequent benign report is adequate. The source meaning matches the stable existing discordance concept.
authorGate.repairRecord: Reuses the existing breast-core discordance meaning despite its historical inflammatory ID. Adds a noninflammatory context without moving FSRS history to a new construct.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Surgery after treatment
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 48-year-old woman, attends clinic after neoadjuvant treatment for noninflammatory left breast cancer. The original mass is no longer palpable. MRI shows a small enhancing remnant around its marker, while mammography shows branching calcifications extending well beyond that remnant into separated breast regions.
sourceLabels: ASBrS breast conserving surgery resource guide, February 2026
Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK
case.learningSummary: A strong enhancement response does not settle the residual calcifications. Representative sampling of their distributed field can determine whether the operation must encompass disease beyond the enhancing remnant. This is an outside diagnostic plan, not an executed clinic order. The sampled sites establish a distributed residual malignant field beyond the small MRI remnant. That current field determines whether a breast-conserving operation can encompass the malignancy. Diffuse malignant calcifications favor mastectomy here; absence of invasion in individual cores is not a whole-breast clearance claim.

steps: Recognize the discrepancy between the residual enhancement and the broader calcification field.
Select the unsolved field for tissue assessment before final operative mapping.
authorGate.closestError: Resample only the enhancing known cancer bed.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Residual calcifications extend into separated regions beyond the enhancing remnant.
authorGate.consequence: Using enhancement alone can under-map residual in-situ disease.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the calcification field were already representatively shown benign and concordant, repeat sampling would no longer be the next task.
authorGate.deletionTest: The broader mammographic field is essential. The absent palpable mass explains why palpation cannot recreate a present tissue target without being the only deciding fact.
authorGate.cueAttack: All labels describe specific tissue assessments and share a biopsy wait. No answer is 'use all information' or 'establish localization' beside deliberately incomplete plans.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Preoperative tissue assessment of residual extent.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: must choose the unresolved residual compartment rather than the most visually active or historically familiar site.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Feedback does not reveal the future calcification histology or prescribe mastectomy.
authorGate.repairRecord: Preserves the response-mapping concept but replaces the no-marker principle question with multimodality evidence requiring an action.

distractorChecks.temptation: Assumes post-treatment enhancement identifies the full residual extent.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: That known cancer bed does not establish whether the calcification field beyond it contains residual malignancy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: If the enhancing focus itself were new or inadequately represented, sampling it would answer a different uncertainty.

distractorChecks.counterfactual: A persisting suspicious palpable target with noncorrelative imaging would require its own representative assessment.

Diffuse malignant calcifications favor mastectomy here; absence of invasion in individual cores is not a whole-breast clearance claim.

steps: Reconcile the separate positive samples with the mammographic distribution beyond the enhancing remnant.
Apply the verified distributed residual field to the operative choice.
authorGate.closestError: Choose a focal or oncoplastic resection based on the small enhancing response.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Malignant samples occupy intervening central and multiple peripheral breast regions.
authorGate.consequence: A limited resection can leave known malignant tissue in the breast.
authorGate.counterfactual: If malignancy were confined to a localized encompassable residual field, conservation could remain appropriate.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing the histologic confirmation or the diffuse map makes the mastectomy key unsupported. The response is retained because it is the credible competing signal.
authorGate.cueAttack: No sentence announces 'conservation is impossible'. All options are specific breast resections. Negative prior radiation prevents importing the old vignette's unsupported blanket radiation conclusion.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Definitive breast resection after completed extent assessment.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: residual histology and distribution must outweigh a reassuring response in a different compartment.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Earlier feedback requires sampling but does not pre-announce the outcome. The new result earns the operation decision.
authorGate.repairRecord: Same conservation-selection meaning, new exact variant. The former vague prior-radiation constraint is replaced with sourced residual-field evidence; no radiation eligibility rule is invented.

distractorChecks.temptation: Uses disappearance of the invasive mass as a surrogate for clearance of all disease.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It follows the MRI response while leaving the broader sampled malignant field outside the excision.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A truly localized residual field with no separate malignant extent could support this operation.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats oncoplastic technique as permission to ignore diffuse malignant distribution.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Resecting the focal sites does not encompass the malignant intervening and peripheral field.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Selected limited multifocal disease that can be encompassed by an appropriate oncologic resection is different.

steps: Recognize that the final specimen contains a substantive invasive component.
Use the invasive-cancer margin standard rather than automatically extending the prior pure-DCIS rule.
authorGate.closestError: Order another re-excision because the DCIS distance remains below 2 mm.
authorGate.decidingObservation: An 8-mm invasive component is present and both components are off the final ink.
authorGate.consequence: Using the wrong framework can cause an unnecessary additional breast operation.
authorGate.counterfactual: If final lateral ink contained carcinoma, further lateral excision would again be favored.
authorGate.deletionTest: The invasive component is essential; remove it and the narrower pure-DCIS decision is individualized rather than the same categorical answer. Imaging clearance prevents a hidden separate target.
authorGate.cueAttack: The update gives measurements and ink observations, not 'adequate margins'. All choices are operations at the same stage. The earlier node's 2-mm counterfactual deliberately creates a credible carry-forward error, not the next key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Need for another breast operation after definitive re-excision pathology.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: applies a changed histologic framework despite the strongly rehearsed DCIS standard.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Later feedback does not reveal axillary or systemic-treatment answers. Each later currentUpdate is an outside-care chart event, not a result generated by an uninstalled service.
authorGate.repairRecord: New meaning under a new concept; do not transfer the old pure-DCIS FSRS history to this invasive-component decision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Carries the earlier DCIS framework forward after the definitive diagnosis changes.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It applies the pure-DCIS width requirement to an invasive carcinoma specimen despite absence of tumor on ink.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Pure DCIS with a clinically consequential close radial margin would require a different case-specific assessment; tumor on ink would favor excision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats two operations and persistent sub-2-mm distance as automatic failure of conservation.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A close but ink-negative DCIS component accompanying invasive cancer is not a stand-alone indication for mastectomy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Diffuse residual malignant disease or unresectable positive margins would change the operation.

case.learningSummary: The initial choice depends on more than whether the primary can be removed. Its HER2-positive biology and regional nodal involvement support neoadjuvant chemotherapy with HER2-directed treatment. The oncology team selects the exact regimen after medical eligibility review. A normal-looking node after treatment is not a pathologic nodal result. In this selected initially cN1, now clinically negative, noninflammatory case, optimized sentinel staging with retrieval of the previously positive clipped node can guide the subsequent axillary decision. A small invasive focus is still residual invasive disease. That finding after taxane/trastuzumab-based therapy supports oncology consideration of ado-trastuzumab emtansine. Clear nodes and clear breast margins answer different questions; the clinic is recommending review, not administering a regimen.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial treatment strategy should the clinic recommend for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Preoperative chemotherapy with HER2-directed therapy
answerChoices.rationale: The HER2-positive, node-positive substantial primary is an established neoadjuvant setting; systemic response can inform later treatment.

answerChoices.label: Breast and axillary surgery followed by systemic therapy
answerChoices.rationale: It bypasses the advantages of the established neoadjuvant strategy in this HER2-positive regional presentation.

answerChoices.label: Preoperative endocrine therapy followed by breast surgery
answerChoices.rationale: The reported tumor lacks hormone receptors and instead has HER2 positivity; endocrine treatment does not address this biology.

answerChoices.label: Dual-tracer sentinel mapping with clipped-node retrieval
answerChoices.rationale: Initially mobile biopsy-proven nodal disease has become clinically negative. The original positive-node marker and optimized mapping permit representative post-treatment staging.

answerChoices.label: Single-tracer sentinel mapping without targeted retrieval
answerChoices.rationale: It omits available techniques that improve reliability in an initially node-positive axilla.

answerChoices.label: Level I–II axillary lymph-node dissection

steps: Reconcile pretreatment biopsy-proven mobile nodal disease with the current clinical response.
Select a representative post-NST staging technique rather than infer ypN0 from ultrasound or mandate ALND from baseline status.
authorGate.closestError: Use a routine single-tracer sentinel operation and leave the previously positive node untargeted.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The clipped node was proven positive before treatment and is clinically negative now; its marker is locatable.
authorGate.consequence: Nonrepresentative staging can miss residual regional disease or lead to unnecessary dissection.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the original nodes had been fixed/matted or remained palpable, ALND would become the offered plan.
authorGate.deletionTest: Remove original biopsy/clip or baseline mobility and the key loses its specific cN1 optimized-staging basis. Current cortical appearance alone cannot resolve the choice.
authorGate.cueAttack: All options are concrete axillary operations. Wait estimates are not used as a correctness cue: these are operative plans, not tests executed by the clinic. The key is similar in length to the competing technical plan.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Axillary operation at definitive surgery after NST.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: distinguishes initial status, apparent response and sample reliability.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Earlier feedback names systemic treatment, not axillary techniques. A later outside pathology update supplies genuinely new residual-disease information.
authorGate.repairRecord: Retires a low-value 'assess both regions' objective by proposal only. New axillary meaning has its own concept; response-mapping history is retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies an uncomplicated upfront sentinel technique to the post-NST cN1 setting.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It omits available techniques that improve reliability in an initially node-positive axilla.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A different initially node-negative setting may not require targeting a previously positive clipped node.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats any pretreatment positive node as an irrevocable dissection indication.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Current cN1 response can permit optimized staging rather than mandatory dissection; the initial nodes were mobile, not bulky/fixed.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Residual palpable disease, initial cN2-3 or inflammatory disease would change this boundary.

authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Choose current recurrent-tumor evidence rather than historical primary or germline evidence for predictive receptor reassessment.
Apply limited sentinel burden and the actual nodal-radiation plan to completion axillary surgery after upfront mastectomy.
Use original nodal status and current response to select representative axillary staging after neoadjuvant therapy.
Retain the pretreatment bulky/fixed nodal boundary despite reassuring current response.
Select representative breast tissue when a skin specimen has not resolved a persistent parenchymal target.
Apply pretreatment clinical phenotype and tissue/staging results to the initial sequence of definitive therapy.
Reconcile the documented marker-to-lesion relation with specimen imaging before deciding whether more tissue should be removed.
Match a persistent nipple epidermal target to representative biopsy tissue despite reassuring parenchymal investigations.
Verify a separate management-changing imaging target rather than treating an unsampled focus as established additional cancer.
Use specimen and needle-position provenance to evaluate a benign sample from a suspicious separate breast target.
Resolve the nature of residual calcifications before using enhancement as the sole operative map.
Use verified residual distribution rather than disappearance of the invasive mass to select the breast operation.
Apply the pure-DCIS margin rule to the actual final radial boundary rather than the main-specimen clearance.
Select the invasive-cancer margin framework when an excision contains invasive carcinoma with associated DCIS.
Use subtype and regional burden to select treatment before definitive surgery.
Distinguish residual invasive disease from imaging response when choosing a specific oncology referral recommendation.
Apply the upfront-conservation limited-node boundary when deciding on completion dissection.
Avoid applying upfront limited-node omission to a residual micrometastasis after NST.

independentReview.title: Receptor reassessment in recurrent breast cancer

cues.phrase: Its receptor studies have not been performed.
cues.why: Names the missing task immediately before asking for receptor reassessment; the only option that fills that named omission is testing the liver core.

cues.phrase: The archived primary's receptor results are in the chart
cues.why: Makes repeating the historical assay look redundant without requiring knowledge of receptor conversion.

cues.phrase: Hereditary breast-cancer panel testing on blood
cues.why: The only option that is not a receptor panel can be rejected by matching the task's 'tumor-receptor' wording.

fairness: Testing the adequate metastatic core is the best offered assessment. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the weakness is discrimination, not a competing correct key.
The current-versus-historical specimen decision is high yield, but the supplied adequacy conclusion and named missing assay reduce this to one obvious selection.

Review scope for this entire report: all 20 after/candidate nodes, including both replacement drafts, were reviewed offline against the supplied authoring standard. No author self-check was treated as evidence of quality, no sources were newly verified, and no clinical approval is granted. Difficulty and high-yield judgments are qualitative. Retained, retired, parked and held records were excluded from node verdicts. Runtime waits, rendering and source provenance were not audited from these visible-content fields.
suggestions: Build a real specimen-selection problem using supported observations about competing samples' timing, viability or assay adequacy; require the learner to decide which evidence can establish current biology.

Compare three plausible tumor-assessment plans, rather than a redundant historical assay and an unrelated germline panel. Preserve necessary specimen information without announcing the unperformed keyed assay.
Remove 'no germline interpretation or metastatic drug regimen is scored here' from learner feedback; it describes authoring scope rather than teaching the clinical distinction.

independentReview.title: Limited positive sentinel nodes after mastectomy with planned regional irradiation
fairness: The intended reasoning is consequential: identify the upfront, limited-burden population, then incorporate planned regional irradiation when deciding about completion dissection. Radiation planning is necessary clinical context, not a wording giveaway.

No completion operation is a defensible best offered answer under the stated omission framework. Contemporary mastectomy omission criteria were not independently verified in this no-network review; clinician confirmation of the exact population remains necessary.

Repeat sentinel mapping and axillary sampling is not a convincing competing plan after four sentinel nodes have already been examined and two are positive. The node effectively presents a binary dissection-versus-omission question with filler.
suggestions: Replace repeat mapping with a clinically credible regional-treatment alternative and broaden the task if necessary so all options address the same decision.
Keep the upfront treatment phase, nodal burden and planned radiation fields explicit; do not remove those necessary eligibility facts to make the question harder.

independentReview.title: Positive sentinel nodes when regional reirradiation is not planned
fairness: Completion dissection is the best offered operation under the supplied radiation constraint. The radiation oncologist's patient-specific assessment appropriately avoids asserting that any prior irradiation universally prohibits reirradiation.
Two real steps remain: identify limited positive nodes after upfront mastectomy, then recognize that the radiation-supported omission pathway cannot simply be transferred to this plan.

Repeat sentinel mapping and axillary sampling again lacks a credible purpose after positive sentinel staging. No confident clinical error was identified in the key, but the third option does not meet the credible-distractor standard.
The exact contemporary omission boundary was not independently source-verified offline.
suggestions: Rebuild the third alternative around an actual competing axillary-treatment decision at this stage; do not retain repeat mapping solely to reach three choices.
Delete the redundant 'No neoadjuvant treatment was given' if 'upfront mastectomy' is retained and is unambiguous for the intended learner.

independentReview.title: Axillary staging after response in an initially node-negative patient
fairness: Sentinel staging is the best offered operation in the represented initially clinically node-negative post-neoadjuvant setting. The explanation correctly separates breast imaging response from pathologic nodal status.

No decisive nonmedical wording shortcut was found, but the breast MRI response is a distractor to an otherwise routine sentinel-staging rule. Normal nodes before and after treatment do not require a second consequential inference here.
This is high-yield foundational knowledge, but the draft is not identified as an independently accepted basic exception.
suggestions: Either seek explicit acceptance as a focused foundational item or replace the simple operation choice with a supported staging-adequacy or phase-dependent problem that changes the next action.
Do not count recognizing a normal axilla and recalling sentinel biopsy as two consequential steps. Remove the breast marker sentence unless a revised task uses it.

independentReview.title: Axillary surgery after response of initially fixed nodal disease
fairness: The pretreatment fixed cluster must be interpreted as a different initial nodal setting from mobile cN1 disease, then carried forward despite apparent response. Clipping and response make targeted staging a credible near-miss.
No lexical cue, convergence pattern or diagnosis label selects dissection without clinical knowledge. Fixed nodes are necessary staging evidence.

Dissection is the best offered plan under the stated standard higher-burden framework. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation's current ASBrS claim was not independently verified offline.

independentReview.title: Tissue diagnosis with progressive breast skin changes

cues.phrase: the parenchymal area has not been sampled
cues.why: Explicitly names the unsampled target while another option repeats the already sampled skin.

cues.phrase: There is no drainable collection.
cues.why: Directly negates the apparent purpose of the aspiration alternative. Together with the named unsampled target, this allows elimination instead of specimen interpretation.

fairness: Image-guided core of the parenchymal abnormality is the best offered next procedure. The negative skin finding does not resolve the breast target; no confident clinical error identified.
The two distractors are weakened by explicit statements that skin was already sampled and no collection is drainable. The inference-to-action chain is largely supplied.
The later invasive-cancer update follows coherently. This explanation does not disclose the next node's systemic-therapy-first sequence.
suggestions: Use a specimen-target adequacy problem with actual acquisition and tissue observations and credible competing tissue procedures. Avoid announcing which target has not been sampled.
Retain the information needed to distinguish solid tissue from a fluid collection, but replace the aspiration foil if it remains plainly inapplicable.

independentReview.title: Initial treatment sequence for inflammatory breast cancer
fairness: The resident must integrate the rapid, extensive skin changes with invasive carcinoma and nonmetastatic staging, then select treatment order. The diagnosis is not supplied as a pre-answer label.

The three options contain the same treatment components in different sequences, avoiding a uniquely comprehensive key. Surgery first is a meaningful error even though radiation first is less tempting.

Systemic therapy before modified radical mastectomy and radiation is the best offered initial strategy. This is a planned sequence, not evidence that surgery will remain appropriate regardless of response.

The update follows the preceding tissue-procedure node, supplies the new pathology and staging, and is understandable with the presentation without needing the prior answer. Earlier feedback does not state this sequence.
suggestions: In feedback, make future surgery conditional on reassessment after systemic therapy; retain the current concrete initial-sequence task.

independentReview.title: Absent biopsy marker despite removal of the calcification target
fairness: The learner must distinguish the documented displaced marker from the malignant target, reconcile specimen and breast imaging, and decide whether further excision is necessary. The absent marker makes unnecessary medial excision a credible error.

Closure while awaiting histologic margins is the best offered plan because the complete mapped calcification target is represented and no residual target is seen. This does not equate radiographic retrieval with negative microscopic margins.

Additional specimen views are less compelling than the marker-bed alternative, but the displacement-versus-retained-target distinction supplies a genuine interpretation task. No nonmedical wording rule alone resolves that distinction.
The record explicitly places the decision before closure, so permanent pathology is not falsely presented as already available. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: For more natural presentation, replace 'The founder reviews' with a named-patient outside intraoperative consultation frame. Keep clear that the operation is ongoing elsewhere and the player is advising from clinic.

independentReview.title: Representative biopsy for a persistent nipple lesion

cues.phrase: the pathology description includes no epidermis
cues.why: Names the missing tissue compartment, followed by a key that uniquely supplies skin.

cues.phrase: Full-thickness biopsy of involved nipple skin
cues.why: It is the only option sampling the visibly involved surface named in the task; both alternatives remain beneath it. Little clinical knowledge is needed once the missing epidermis is announced.

fairness: Representative nipple skin biopsy is the best offered procedure. Negative parenchymal imaging and a benign subareolar core do not exclude a nipple epidermal process.
The explanation appropriately allows an adequate punch or wedge rather than falsely ranking the two. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
Persistent nipple disease is highly testable, but this particular tissue-compartment matching exercise is one-step recognition, not a difficult resident application.
suggestions: Either obtain explicit foundational-item acceptance or test a real specimen-adequacy/extent decision in which several plausible samples have useful but different evidentiary limits.
Do not merely delete the missing-epidermis statement while leaving an underspecified specimen; rebuild the comparison so necessary raw tissue findings require interpretation.

independentReview.title: Verification of a separate MRI breast finding

cues.phrase: only the 10-o'clock lesion has been sampled
cues.why: Identifies the completed task, making the option that samples the other clock position the unique new diagnostic action.

cues.phrase: The additional focus would change the planned breast resection.
cues.why: Supplies the management-changing interpretation rather than requiring it; combined with 'before the breast operation is changed,' it rehearses the reason for the key.

cues.phrase: The radiologist can target both findings
cues.why: A feasibility permission removes any practical target-selection problem while repeating the procedure's rationale.

fairness: Biopsy of the separate suspicious focus before escalating surgery is the best offered procedure. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
Repeating the proven primary's biopsy has no supplied adequacy or discordance problem. Interval MRI and the completed-target repeat do not create two consequential steps.

The following node coherently supplies a biopsy attempt, but this explanation's instruction to assess whether tissue fits the target scaffolds that later concordance task. It does not supply the actual later needle-position interpretation.
suggestions: Present the concrete planned resection and spatial imaging observations so the learner infers why the second finding matters.
Replace the redundant primary biopsy with a credible diagnostic alternative or redesign the node around competing acquisition/target problems. Keep any genuinely necessary feasibility fact neutral.
Keep this feedback focused on verification before escalation; let the later node earn its separate concordance inference.

independentReview.title: Benign tissue from a biopsy that missed the MRI target
fairness: The learner must reconcile benign adipose tissue with a needle notch and marker posterior to a persistent focus, then choose repeat representative sampling instead of accepting the benign label or treating unproven multicentric malignancy.
Repeat image-guided sampling is the best offered plan. A benign report does not establish benignity of a target the needle did not represent. No confident clinical error identified.

The options reflect two meaningful opposite errors: premature reassurance and premature oncologic escalation. No key-only lexical match or convergence selects the answer without interpreting target representation.

The update is coherent after the first diagnostic plan and stands with the shared presentation. Previous feedback primes concordance generally, so difficulty is moderate, not hard; it does not disclose this acquisition failure.
suggestions: For maximal precision, change 'The 4-o'clock focus is sampled' to describe a biopsy attempt targeting that focus, since the subsequent evidence shows that the focus itself was missed.

independentReview.title: Operative mapping of calcifications beyond an MRI remnant
clarityIssues: The original distribution and prior tissue assessment of the calcifications are absent. It is unclear whether this is an uncharacterized field needing diagnostic mapping or already established malignant extent. That distinction matters to the purpose of another biopsy.

cues.phrase: The original mass is no longer palpable.
cues.why: Directly disables the palpation-guided alternative rather than leaving a credible competing tissue-assessment plan.

cues.phrase: extending well beyond that remnant into separated breast regions
cues.why: Together with the task's 'operative map,' this favors the only option covering the distributed field. The other options both stay at the original mass.

fairness: The underlying high-yield lesson is that MRI enhancement response does not establish clearance of residual calcifications.

Field sampling is plausible, but the stem does not establish how these calcifications relate to the pretreatment cancer map or why further biopsy is needed before surgical planning. I cannot confidently validate the exact diagnostic workflow from these fields alone.

Do not imply that negative selected cores would automatically permit leaving all suspicious post-treatment calcifications. The current explanation does not explicitly claim this, but its 'determine whether the operation must encompass disease' wording needs clinician scrutiny.
The next node supplies actual malignant mapping results and follows the proposed procedure; the first explanation does not explicitly name its mastectomy answer.
suggestions: State the relevant prior calcification map and pathology, and identify the unresolved extent question that a new tissue assessment would answer.
Have the clinician verify the exact post-neoadjuvant calcification workup and surgical-extent implication; do not invent a sampling threshold or negative-biopsy clearance rule.
Replace palpation of a nonpalpable target with a credible image-guided alternative, and make the choice depend on interpreting the records rather than matching field size.
Remove the explanation's software-oriented 'not an executed clinic order' sentence from learner teaching.

independentReview.title: Breast surgery for distributed residual malignant calcifications
clarityIssues: 'Tissue between the original foci' and 'original focal tumor sites' introduce multiple original foci, whereas the shared presentation describes an original mass and its marker without a pretreatment multifocal map.

The oncoplastic option is limited to original focal sites rather than clearly describing whether it attempts to encompass the newly demonstrated malignant field. That makes the apparent conservation alternative narrower than the real surgical question.

cues.phrase: Localized excision of the marked enhancing bed
cues.why: Like the other conservation option, it explicitly ignores the newly mapped central and peripheral disease. Comparing a whole-breast operation with two old-target operations weakens the intended feasibility judgment.

fairness: Mastectomy is the best offered operation for the described diffuse malignant field, and the explanation correctly avoids treating no invasion in sampled cores as proof of whole-breast clearance.

Two meaningful steps are available: interpret the distributed DCIS despite the small MRI remnant, then apply the current extent to the operation. The ambiguous original-foci history and restricted conservation labels blunt that reasoning.

The new pathology follows the preceding mapping plan and can be interpreted with the presentation. Earlier feedback establishes that calcifications matter but does not explicitly give this operation. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: Make the original lesion map consistent across both nodes, or remove references to undocumented original foci.

Describe actual current field geometry and its relationship to the breast sufficiently to compare mastectomy with a credible attempt to remove the entire malignant distribution. Do not manufacture an exact breast-volume cutoff.
Do not use two knowingly incomplete old-target excisions as substitutes for a realistic conservation decision.

independentReview.title: Final cavity margin despite clear main lumpectomy margins
fairness: The learner must reconstruct which oriented specimen defines the final lateral boundary, then treat tumor at that inked boundary despite reassuring main-specimen distances.

Re-excision before radiation is the best offered plan. Remaining parenchyma, nondiffuse extent and the patient's conservation preference appropriately distinguish it from accepting the positive margin or choosing mastectomy.
The lateral wording identifies the anatomical site; it does not itself establish why the additional shave supersedes the main specimen. No material key-only cue or convergence shortcut found.
The later re-excision and definitive combined histology follow coherently. This explanation does not teach the subsequent invasive-with-DCIS margin rule. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

independentReview.title: Margin framework after invasive carcinoma is found with DCIS
fairness: The combined specimens change the diagnosis from pure DCIS to invasive carcinoma with associated DCIS. The learner must change the applicable margin framework, then decide whether the close but ink-negative lateral edge needs another excision.

No additional breast excision is the best offered margin-specific answer given clear ink, no residual suspicious calcifications and planned whole-breast radiation. Another excision is a credible error if the learner carries forward the pure-DCIS rule.
The update supplies the new histology and final margins without requiring the previous answer. It follows the re-excision node and preserves patient, side and treatment chronology.

The task appropriately limits itself to breast surgery for this margin; it does not imply that newly identified invasion needs no other staging or management. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

independentReview.title: Initial treatment of node-positive HER2-positive breast cancer

cues.phrase: HER2 immunostaining is 3+
cues.why: Only the keyed option repeats HER2. The surgery-first option uses generic 'systemic therapy,' so a reader can favor the uniquely biomarker-matched label without deciding treatment order.

fairness: The intended two-step reasoning is appropriate: interpret receptor results and regional disease, then select neoadjuvant systemic treatment rather than upfront surgery.

Preoperative chemotherapy with HER2-directed therapy is the best offered strategy. Endocrine treatment is not a competitive plan with the explicitly ER/PR-negative tumor; the draft leaves only one strong distractor.
The explanation appropriately defers exact regimen selection to medical eligibility review. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The later response/staging and residual-disease nodes follow this therapy coherently. This feedback does not give either later operation or adjuvant drug.
suggestions: Hold the HER2-directed systemic components constant across credible sequencing alternatives so the learner must use stage and treatment timing, rather than unique biomarker word matching.
Replace the endocrine foil with a clinician-supported plausible strategy for this tumor biology; do not add a known-inapplicable therapy simply to reach three options.

independentReview.title: Axillary staging after response of initially mobile node-positive disease

cues.phrase: Single-tracer sentinel mapping without targeted retrieval
cues.why: The 'without' label advertises an omitted component while the key offers both dual mapping and retrieval. It makes the key the visibly more complete version of the same procedure.

cues.phrase: The operative localization record identifies that clip
cues.why: In combination with the deliberately incomplete mapping foil, the repeated clip/retrieval wording makes it easy to match the documented object to the comprehensive option. The clip itself is necessary clinical information and should not simply be deleted.

fairness: The intended two steps are sound: recognize the initially mobile node-positive to clinically negative transition, then select an appropriate staging approach rather than infer pathologic clearance or automatically dissect.

Targeted optimized staging is a defensible best offered approach for this selected scenario. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Detailed current technical adequacy requirements were not independently source-verified offline.

The update follows the initial systemic-therapy decision, and the shared presentation supplies initial nodal status. It stands without the prior answer. Its explanation does not reveal the later adjuvant drug.
suggestions: Remove critique-style 'without targeted retrieval' wording and compare neutrally described, genuinely plausible operative strategies.

For a stronger application item, use actual mapping/retrieval observations that require assessment of staging adequacy before a next action. Verify any exact technical criterion with the clinician and supporting source; do not invent a node-count rule.
Retain the initial mobile-node findings, current response and clip history because those determine which evidence applies.

independentReview.title: Adjuvant therapy after residual invasive HER2-positive disease
fairness: The learner must distinguish a small residual invasive focus from nodal clearance, clear margins or residual DCIS alone, then apply the post-neoadjuvant treatment implication. Continuing trastuzumab is a credible competing error.

Ado-trastuzumab emtansine is the best offered option under the established residual-invasive-disease framework after taxane/trastuzumab therapy. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The changing contemporary HER2 treatment landscape was not independently verified in this no-network review.

The drug labels are comparable and no unique word match selects the key: trastuzumab appears in both the key and the continuation option. Neratinib is less competitive at this treatment stage, but it is a recognizable HER2-treatment sequencing error.

This third node supplies prior treatment, current surgery and residual histology, so it stands with the presentation without relying on earlier answers. Earlier explanations do not disclose this drug.

originalReview.title: Residual micrometastatic nodal disease after neoadjuvant therapy
clarityIssues: 'The axilla is no longer palpable' should refer to the previously palpable axillary node or nodes, not the axilla itself.
fairness: Two consequential steps are required: interpret the small deposit as residual nodal disease after neoadjuvant treatment despite apparently adequate targeted retrieval, then avoid importing upfront-surgery omission criteria merely because nodal radiation is planned.

Completion dissection with planned radiation is the best offered answer under the stated conventional post-neoadjuvant residual-disease framework. Radiation without dissection is a strong near-miss. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The exact current management boundary for post-neoadjuvant micrometastases is evolving and was not independently verified offline. Treat 'current standard guidance' as requiring dated clinician/source confirmation, not as validated by this review.

Repeat targeted sentinel surgery is poorly motivated after the clipped node and multiple sentinel nodes have already been retrieved. The third option should represent a genuine competing management error rather than repeat completed staging.
No lexical cue or convergence pattern chooses between the two meaningful treatment plans. Difficulty comes from treatment phase and residual burden, not from the wording repair needed.
suggestions: Correct the palpable-node wording and replace the repeat-staging foil with a credible treatment-stage alternative, preserving the difficult dissection-versus-radiation comparison.

Have Melissa confirm the exact dated guideline boundary and any relevant trial-versus-standard distinction before accepting the teaching point; do not infer a universal rule from older upfront-surgery data.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic with new liver lesions after treatment of an ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. The outside liver core contains metastatic breast carcinoma with sufficient viable tumor for additional assays. Its receptor studies have not been performed. The archived primary's receptor results are in the chart, and her systemic treatment is being reconsidered.

case.learningSummary: The current core is adequate tumor tissue from the recurrence. Use it to reassess predictive receptor status rather than assume the original phenotype persists. Hereditary testing answers a separate question; no germline interpretation or metastatic drug regimen is scored here.

decisionNodes.stem: Which laboratory assessment should guide {patientName}'s current tumor-receptor reassessment?

answerChoices.label: ER, PR and HER2 testing on the liver core
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate current tumor can establish the recurrence's predictive phenotype; the archived primary does not prove that phenotype is unchanged.

answerChoices.label: ER, PR and HER2 testing on the archived breast specimen
answerChoices.rationale: It reassesses the historical primary rather than establishing the present metastatic tumor's phenotype.

answerChoices.label: Hereditary breast-cancer panel testing on blood
answerChoices.rationale: A germline panel addresses inherited susceptibility, not expression of predictive receptors in the current carcinoma.

steps: Interpret acid processing outside assay validation as a limitation on the negative metastatic profile, rather than proof of receptor conversion.
Choose the viable nondecalcified current metastasis instead of either accepting that profile or retreating to historical tumor biology.
authorGate.closestError: Accept the latest bone receptor report because current tissue should normally outrank the primary.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The negative bone profile followed an unvalidated decalcification process, while a nondecalcified current metastatic block is available.
authorGate.consequence: A technically uncertain negative profile can be mistaken for a biological treatment target change.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the bone sample had validated processing and reliable assays, a discordant current metastatic profile could legitimately guide treatment.
authorGate.deletionTest: Deleting the processing record removes the reason to question the current bone profile; deleting the liver provenance makes the selected current evidence unavailable. No missing assay is announced.
authorGate.cueAttack: All three plans concern the same tumor receptor evidence. Removed the germline foil and the named unperformed assay. Current bone, current liver and historical primary each offer a real but different evidentiary temptation.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Laboratory evidence plan before changing systemic treatment.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: current-versus-historical evidence must be reconciled with preanalytic reliability, not just tissue availability.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revision; no earlier feedback supplies the processing interpretation or choice.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision addresses every review cue. New concept version explicitly records the material addition of assay-validity interpretation; prior FSRS history is retained.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes specimen recency without interpreting processing-related uncertainty.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A current specimen is normally valuable, but the negative profile cannot be treated as settled conversion when the actual decalcification process is outside assay validation and suitable alternative tissue exists.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A technically reliable current metastatic assay can guide therapy even if it differs from the old primary.

distractorChecks.temptation: Escapes a technically questionable current result by returning to the familiar primary.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It can confirm historical biology but cannot resolve whether the recurrence has genuinely changed phenotype.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A question about the original assay itself would appropriately use the original block.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Removed the named missing assay, adequacy conclusion and unrelated germline option. Compared a current negative bone report, current nondecalcified metastatic tissue and historical primary tissue. The processing/validation record is the deciding evidence; current results can still govern if technically reliable. Removed software/scope language from feedback. ASCO specimen-processing guidance was directly verified and recorded with reserved rights.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Completion axillary review
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 62-year-old woman, attends clinic after upfront mastectomy and sentinel biopsy for a 2.8-cm noninflammatory invasive cancer. Her axilla was clinically negative before surgery. Two of four sentinel nodes contain metastases; there is no gross extranodal disease. The radiation oncologist has planned postmastectomy chest-wall and regional nodal irradiation, and systemic therapy is planned.
sourceLabels: ASBrS axillary management resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: Mastectomy does not impose an unconditional completion-ALND rule. In selected upfront cases with limited positive sentinel burden, planned regional nodal irradiation can support omission. This is a radiation-dependent decision and should not be applied to post-NST residual nodes.

decisionNodes.stem: Which further axillary operation should be recommended for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: No completion axillary operation
answerChoices.rationale: Selected upfront mastectomy patients with one or two positive sentinel nodes can omit ALND when the adjuvant plan includes regional nodal irradiation.

answerChoices.label: Completion level I–II axillary dissection
answerChoices.rationale: It treats mastectomy plus any positive sentinel finding as an unconditional ALND requirement, despite the stated limited burden and nodal irradiation.

answerChoices.label: Repeat sentinel mapping and axillary sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The completed representative sentinel procedure already establishes the relevant limited burden; repeat staging is not a substitute for interpreting that information.

steps: Identify the upfront clinically node-negative, limited positive-sentinel population.
Apply the actual nodal radiation component and morbidity goal to distinguish the supported omission pathway from extra surgery or inadequate field de-escalation.
authorGate.closestError: Treat the chest-wall field as equivalent to chest-wall plus regional nodal irradiation after mastectomy.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Only two sentinel nodes are involved and a regional nodal field is actually planned.
authorGate.consequence: A field mistake can remove the basis for omission, while automatically combining treatments adds avoidable morbidity.
authorGate.counterfactual: If regional nodal irradiation were ruled out, the offered radiation-only omission plan would no longer apply.
authorGate.deletionTest: The nodal burden and precise field are both necessary. The morbidity goal distinguishes an appropriate omission pathway from adding a redundant operation.
authorGate.cueAttack: All choices are concrete locoregional treatment plans. Repeat mapping is gone; radiation appears in every option, so the task's locoregional wording does not uniquely match the key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Postmastectomy locoregional treatment rather than repeated staging.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted fair moderate: the nearest field and surgery errors are credible; no harder rating is manufactured from an ordinary limited-node rule.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revised case; no unchanged PASS presentation is modified.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision broadens options to genuine regional-treatment strategies and keeps the reviewed population/field criteria explicit. Meaning remains the radiation-dependent axillary boundary.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies a positive-node surgery rule despite a radiation-supported omission population.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Adding dissection to the already applicable regional radiation plan is not required by these two positive sentinel nodes and works against the stated morbidity goal.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Residual disease after NST or a different higher-burden presentation can require a surgical regional approach.

distractorChecks.temptation: Transfers limited-node breast-conservation de-escalation to mastectomy while overlooking its different radiation context.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It drops the nodal-treatment component on which this mastectomy omission pathway depends.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A node-negative mastectomy patient with an independent chest-wall indication would present a different field question.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Retained upfront phase, limited node burden and actual nodal field. Replaced repeat staging with three locoregional treatment policies: the planned field, addition of dissection, or chest-wall-only de-escalation. A patient morbidity/control goal distinguishes gratuitous combined therapy from the supported radiation pathway. Current ASBrS population and NCI morbidity evidence were rechecked; no new clinical approval claimed.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Axillary response review
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 50-year-old woman, attends clinic after neoadjuvant treatment for noninflammatory breast cancer. The pretreatment surgeon documented a fixed cluster of axillary nodes, and a core contained metastatic carcinoma. A node was clipped. authorGate.sequenceCheck: The first node feedback establishes diagnosis needs without giving this sequence. No hypothetical future response is treated as an observed response.
authorGate.repairRecord: Same sequence concept; repairs the original set's omitted-radiation and lumpectomy caricatures without touching the frozen B37-context variant.

distractorChecks.temptation: Prioritizes immediate resection of an operable primary before systemic treatment.

case.displayName: Clinic chart review: Review breast extent
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 57-year-old woman, attends clinic with a biopsy-proven left invasive carcinoma at 10 o'clock. Mammography and ultrasound show one localized lesion. MRI also shows a separate irregular enhancing focus at 4 o'clock. The radiologist can target both findings; only the 10-o'clock lesion has been sampled. The additional focus would change the planned breast resection.
sourceLabels: Clinical guidance for breast cancer screening assessment — GOV.UK
ASBrS breast conserving surgery resource guide, February 2026
case.learningSummary: One proven cancer does not make every separate enhancing focus malignant. Sample the additional management-changing target before escalating the operation on its account, then assess whether its tissue result fits that target. A benign report is not independent of its target. The needle position and adipose specimen leave the irregular focus unrepresented. Resolve that focus with representative tissue before either dismissing it or using it to justify a larger cancer operation.

case.learningSummary: A strong enhancement response does not settle the residual calcifications. Representative sampling of their distributed field can determine whether the operation must encompass disease beyond the enhancing remnant. This is an outside diagnostic plan, not an executed clinic order. The sampled sites establish a distributed residual malignant field beyond the small MRI remnant. That current field determines whether a breast-conserving operation can encompass the malignancy. Diffuse malignant calcifications favor mastectomy here; absence of invasion in individual cores is not a whole-breast clearance claim.

authorGate.closestError: Proceed to radiation using the main specimen's 3-mm distance.
authorGate.decidingObservation: DCIS reaches the marked external ink of the additional lateral shave.
authorGate.consequence: Treating the main specimen as final can leave an involved radial boundary untreated surgically.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the additional shave's external edge were 2 mm clear with the same localized imaging, proceed to radiation rather than re-excise.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the shave orientation and ink observation, the apparently adequate main specimen supports the competing plan. Radial residual parenchyma prevents misapplication of a skin/fascia exception.
authorGate.cueAttack: The complaint and task do not call the margin positive. All choices are complete local-treatment sequences; no option advertises an omitted safety action. The main-specimen measurement supports a credible shortcut.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Next definitive local-treatment plan after final pathology.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: final-specimen hierarchy competes with an adequate main margin, not two competing memorized widths.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: First node. Feedback does not state the invasive-cancer margin rule used by the later node.
authorGate.repairRecord: Reuses the stable DCIS margin meaning; replaces a 2-mm recall item with a final-boundary application. No existing definition is overwritten.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies the adequate main-specimen distance to the wrong final boundary.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The main specimen's clearance does not cancel tumor on the new radial boundary; planned radiation does not establish surgical clearance.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: If the oriented final lateral boundary were adequately clear, this would be appropriate.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats any residual DCIS as failure of the entire conservation pathway.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: An addressable positive radial margin is not itself a requirement for mastectomy when disease is localized and breast preservation remains intended.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Diffuse malignant distribution or persistent uncorrectable margins could make mastectomy appropriate.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

steps: Recognize that the final specimen contains a substantive invasive component.
Use the invasive-cancer margin standard rather than automatically extending the prior pure-DCIS rule.
authorGate.closestError: Order another re-excision because the DCIS distance remains below 2 mm.
authorGate.decidingObservation: An 8-mm invasive component is present and both components are off the final ink.
authorGate.consequence: Using the wrong framework can cause an unnecessary additional breast operation.
authorGate.counterfactual: If final lateral ink contained carcinoma, further lateral excision would again be favored.
authorGate.deletionTest: The invasive component is essential; remove it and the narrower pure-DCIS decision is individualized rather than the same categorical answer. Imaging clearance prevents a hidden separate target.
authorGate.cueAttack: The update gives measurements and ink observations, not 'adequate margins'. All choices are operations at the same stage. The earlier node's 2-mm counterfactual deliberately creates a credible carry-forward error, not the next key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Need for another breast operation after definitive re-excision pathology.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: applies a changed histologic framework despite the strongly rehearsed DCIS standard.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Later feedback does not reveal axillary or systemic-treatment answers. Each later currentUpdate is an outside-care chart event, not a result generated by an uninstalled service.
authorGate.repairRecord: New meaning under a new concept; do not transfer the old pure-DCIS FSRS history to this invasive-component decision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Carries the earlier DCIS framework forward after the definitive diagnosis changes.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It applies the pure-DCIS width requirement to an invasive carcinoma specimen despite absence of tumor on ink.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Pure DCIS with a clinically consequential close radial margin would require a different case-specific assessment; tumor on ink would favor excision.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats two operations and persistent sub-2-mm distance as automatic failure of conservation.

authorGate.closestError: Infer that if axillary dissection can be omitted, partial-breast irradiation can also replace whole-breast treatment.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Pathologically positive sentinel tissue coexists with otherwise eligible upfront conservation criteria.
authorGate.consequence: Combining unrelated de-escalation rules can place the patient outside the supporting treatment population.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the nodes were pathologically negative and the other APBI criteria were met, partial-breast treatment could become a reasonable plan.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing nodal positivity changes both the surgical interpretation and partial-breast eligibility. The radiation comparison is no longer pre-decided by a declared plan.
authorGate.cueAttack: Corrected palpable-node anatomy. Three actual locoregional courses replace repeat sentinel staging; components recur across options and none is a uniquely cautious omnibus plan.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Locoregional completion treatment after upfront lumpectomy.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted moderate/hard: distinguishes two interacting but noninterchangeable de-escalation decisions.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone, with no preceding postoperative-NST explanation to supply the boundary.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision removes the filler and fixes clarity. Explicit new concept version preserves the prior narrower axillary-surgery history because radiation-eligibility interpretation is now scored.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats every sentinel macrometastasis as a completion-dissection indication.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It applies an automatic dissection rule despite the eligible limited-burden upfront conservation setting.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Heavier nodal burden or post-NST residual metastasis can change the surgical indication.

distractorChecks.temptation: Combines two attractive de-escalations as if omission of dissection proved partial-breast eligibility.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It substitutes a partial-breast-only plan despite pathologically positive nodes, outside routine APBI eligibility.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An otherwise suitable node-negative patient may be a partial-breast candidate after separate assessment.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Corrected the palpable-node wording. Replaced repeated mapping with an actual partial-breast versus whole-breast completion policy alongside dissection. Nodal positivity now matters to both de-escalation boundaries. The third policy has direct APBI eligibility support; exact radiation fields are not invented. A new concept version records the materially broader radiation-eligibility objective.

steps: Interpret the measured deposit as residual micrometastasis despite successful retrieval and a reassuring examination.
Apply the post-NST residual-node indication rather than either upfront-surgery radiation substitution or omission.
authorGate.closestError: Replace dissection with axillary radiation because the deposit is small and was removed in a mapped node.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The 0.9-mm metastasis remains after neoadjuvant therapy, not at an upfront conservation operation.
authorGate.consequence: Cross-population extrapolation can omit the regional operation recommended for residual disease.
authorGate.counterfactual: The analogous limited sentinel finding at upfront conservation could support no completion operation; an adequate ypN0 result after NST also changes the decision.
authorGate.deletionTest: Both measured burden and treatment chronology matter. Palpation is corrected to nodes and cannot overrule the positive specimen.
authorGate.cueAttack: Three real axillary treatment policies replace repeated completed staging. Shared whole-breast treatment stays outside options, so the key is not uniquely comprehensive or uniquely linked to radiation wording.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Additional regional treatment after pathological post-NST staging.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted hard: the strongest error is a plausible radiation-based de-escalation supported in a different phase.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revised case; no prior feedback supplies the boundary. Its dated source check is recorded separately from clinician approval.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision fixes anatomy, replaces the staging filler and positively states the sourced residual-micrometastasis indication; clinical review remains pending.

distractorChecks.temptation: Transfers an upfront axillary-radiation alternative to a residual post-treatment positive node.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It replaces the currently recommended completion operation with a radiation alternative whose equivalence in this post-NST residual setting is not established by the retrieved guide.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An eligible upfront-surgery patient with limited sentinel involvement can have a different regional-radiation pathway.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treats a small deposit plus normal palpation as sufficient for the upfront limited-node omission pathway.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It carries the upfront conservation omission rule across to documented residual disease after NST.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: The comparable limited positive-sentinel finding at upfront conservation with appropriate radiation can permit no further axillary operation.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

beforeAfter.reviewResponse: Corrected palpability to axillary nodes, kept the measured deposit and adequate retrieval, and replaced repeat staging with no additional axillary treatment. The positive residual-micrometastasis indication was rechecked in the February 2026 ASBrS guide; Melissa review remains pending.

steps: Identify the upfront clinically node-negative, limited positive-sentinel population.
Apply the actual nodal radiation component and morbidity goal to distinguish the supported omission pathway from extra surgery or inadequate field de-escalation.
authorGate.closestError: Treat the chest-wall field as equivalent to chest-wall plus regional nodal irradiation after mastectomy.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Only two sentinel nodes are involved and a regional nodal field is actually planned.
authorGate.consequence: A field mistake can remove the basis for omission, while automatically combining treatments adds avoidable morbidity.
authorGate.counterfactual: If regional nodal irradiation were ruled out, the offered radiation-only omission plan would no longer apply.
authorGate.deletionTest: The nodal burden and precise field are both necessary. The morbidity goal distinguishes an appropriate omission pathway from adding a redundant operation.
authorGate.cueAttack: All choices are concrete locoregional treatment plans. Repeat mapping is gone; radiation appears in every option, so the task's locoregional wording does not uniquely match the key.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Postmastectomy locoregional treatment rather than repeated staging.
authorGate.difficulty: Predicted fair moderate: the nearest field and surgery errors are credible; no harder rating is manufactured from an ordinary limited-node rule.
authorGate.sequenceCheck: Standalone revised case; no unchanged PASS presentation is modified.
authorGate.repairRecord: One revision broadens options to genuine regional-treatment strategies and keeps the reviewed population/field criteria explicit. Meaning remains the radiation-dependent axillary boundary.

distractorChecks.temptation: Applies a positive-node surgery rule despite a radiation-supported omission population.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Adding dissection to the already applicable regional radiation plan is not required by these two positive sentinel nodes and works against the stated morbidity goal.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Residual disease after NST or a different higher-burden presentation can require a surgical regional approach.

distractorChecks.temptation: Transfers limited-node breast-conservation de-escalation to mastectomy while overlooking its different radiation context.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: It drops the nodal-treatment component on which this mastectomy omission pathway depends.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A node-negative mastectomy patient with an independent chest-wall indication would present a different field question.

constructedObservations.basis: Fixed fictional observations. No new empirical frequencies, medication rules or clinical thresholds.

currentBeforeAfter.reviewResponse: Retained upfront phase, limited node burden and actual nodal field. Replaced repeat staging with three locoregional treatment policies: the planned field, addition of dissection, or chest-wall-only de-escalation. A patient morbidity/control goal distinguishes gratuitous combined therapy from the supported radiation pathway. Current ASBrS population and NCI morbidity evidence were rechecked; no new clinical approval claimed.
